1.74.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
athocyante hanumato mantrāḥ sarveṣṭadāyakāḥ /
yānsamārādhya viprendra tattulyācaraṇā narāḥ //
1.74.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथोच्यन्ते हनुमतो मन्त्राः सर्वेष्टदायकाः ।
यान्समाराध्य विप्रेन्द्र तत्तुल्याचरणा नराः ॥
1.74.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now the mantras of Hanumān that bestow all desires are spoken of, / by worshipping which, O best of brahmins, men come to act like him.

1.74.s:
manuḥ svaredusaṃyuktaṃ gaganaṃ ca bhagānvitāḥ /
hasaphaāgniniśādhīśāḥdvitīyaṃ bījamīritam //
1.74.d:
मनुः स्वरेदुसंयुक्तं गगनं च भगान्विताः ।
हसफआग्निनिशाधीशाःद्वितीयं बीजमीरितम् ॥
1.74.m: The mantra: ether joined with vowel and moon, and combined with ‘bhaga’; / ‘ha’, ‘sa’, ‘pha’, fire, and the lord of the night: this is declared as the second seed-syllable;

1.74.s:
svaphaāgnayo bhagendvāḍhyāstṛtīyaṃ bījamīritam /
viyadbhṛgvagnimanvinduyuktaṃ syāñca caturthakam //
1.74.d:
स्वफआग्नयो भगेन्द्वाढ्यास्तृतीयं बीजमीरितम् ।
वियद्भृग्वग्निमन्विन्दुयुक्तं स्याञ्च चतुर्थकम् ॥
1.74.m: ‘sva’, ‘pha’, and fires, rich in ‘bhaga’ and the moon: this is declared as the third seed-syllable; / ether, Bhṛgu, fire, Manu, and the moon combined shall be the fourth;

1.74.s:
pañcamaṃ bhagacandrāḍhyāviyadbhṛgusvakāgnayaḥ /
manvindvāḍhyau hasau ṣaṣṭaṃ ṅeṃtaḥ syāddhanumāṃstataḥ //
1.74.d:
पञ्चमं भगचन्द्राढ्यावियद्भृगुस्वकाग्नयः ।
मन्विन्द्वाढ्यौ हसौ षष्टं ङेंतः स्याद्धनुमांस्ततः ॥
1.74.m: the fifth is ‘bhaga’ and moon, joined with ether, Bhṛgu, its own [vowel], and fire; / ‘ha’ and ‘sa’ joined with Manu and moon is the sixth; then ‘hanumat’ in the dative;

1.74.s:
hṛdayānto mahāmantrarājo 'yaṃ dvādaśākṣaraḥ /
rāmacandro muniścāsya jagatīchanda īritam //
1.74.d:
हृदयान्तो महामन्त्रराजो ऽयं द्वादशाक्षरः ।
रामचन्द्रो मुनिश्चास्य जगतीछन्द ईरितम् ॥
1.74.m: ending with ‘hṛdaya’—this twelve-syllabled [formula] is the king of great mantras. / Rāmacandra is its sage, and Jagatī is declared as the metre;

1.74.s:
devatā hanumānbījaṃ ṣaṣṭaṃ śaktirdvatīyakam /
ṣaḍbījaiśca ṣaḍaṅgāni śirobhāle dṛśormukhe //
1.74.d:
देवता हनुमान्बीजं षष्टं शक्तिर्द्वतीयकम् ।
षड्बीजैश्च षडङ्गानि शिरोभाले दृशोर्मुखे ॥
1.74.m: Hanumān is the deity, the sixth is the seed-syllable, the second is the power. / And with the six seed-syllables, the six limbs [are placed]: on the head, on the forehead, on the two eyes, in the mouth,

1.74.s:
galabāhudvaye caiva hṛdi kukṣau ca nābhitaḥ /
dhvaje jānudvaye pādadvaye varṇānkramānnyaset //
1.74.d:
गलबाहुद्वये चैव हृदि कुक्षौ च नाभितः ।
ध्वजे जानुद्वये पादद्वये वर्णान्क्रमान्न्यसेत् ॥
1.74.m: on the throat and two arms, on the heart and belly, at the navel, / on the penis, on the two knees, and on the two feet, one should place the syllables in order.

1.74.s:
ṣaḍbījāni padadvandvaṃ mūrdhni bhāle mukhe hṛdi /
nābhāvūrvorjaṅghayośca pādayorvinyasetkramāt //
1.74.d:
षड्बीजानि पदद्वन्द्वं मूर्ध्नि भाले मुखे हृदि ।
नाभावूर्वोर्जङ्घयोश्च पादयोर्विन्यसेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.74.m: One should place the six seed-syllables and the two words in order: on the crown, on the forehead, in the mouth, on the heart, / at the navel, on the thighs, on the shanks, and on the feet.

1.74.s:
añjanīgarbhasaṃbhūtaṃ tato dhyāyetkapīśvaram /
udyatkoṭyarkasaṃkāśaṃ jagatprakṣobhakārakam //
1.74.d:
अञ्जनीगर्भसंभूतं ततो ध्यायेत्कपीश्वरम् ।
उद्यत्कोट्यर्कसंकाशं जगत्प्रक्षोभकारकम् ॥
1.74.m: Then one should meditate upon the lord of monkeys, born from the womb of Añjanī, / resembling ten million rising suns, shaking the world,

1.74.s:
śrīrāmāṅghridhyānaniṣṭaṃ sugrīvapramukhārcitam /
vitrāsayantaṃ nādena rākṣasānmārutiṃ bhajet //
1.74.d:
श्रीरामाङ्घ्रिध्याननिष्टं सुग्रीवप्रमुखार्चितम् ।
वित्रासयन्तं नादेन राक्षसान्मारुतिं भजेत् ॥
1.74.m: devoted to meditating on the feet of glorious Rāma, worshipped by Sugrīva and others; / one should resort to Māruti, who terrifies the rākṣasas with his roar.

1.74.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapedbhānusahasraṃ vijitaindriyaḥ /
daśāṃśaṃ juhuyādbīhīnpayodadhyājyamiśritān //
1.74.d:
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेद्भानुसहस्रं विजितैन्द्रियः ।
दशांशं जुहुयाद्बीहीन्पयोदध्याज्यमिश्रितान् ॥
1.74.m: Having meditated thus, one should recite twelve thousand times, with senses conquered. / One should offer into the fire a tenth [part in] paddy mixed with milk, curd, and clarified butter.

1.74.s:
pūrvokte vaiṣṇave pīṭhe mūrttiṃ saṃkalpya mūlataḥ /
āvāhya tatra saṃpūjya pādyādibhirupāyanaiḥ //
1.74.d:
पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवे पीठे मूर्त्तिं संकल्प्य मूलतः ।
आवाह्य तत्र संपूज्य पाद्यादिभिरुपायनैः ॥
1.74.m: Having fashioned an image with the root [mantra] upon the previously mentioned Vaiṣṇava ritual seat, / invoking [him] there and worshipping with water for the feet and other offerings,

1.74.s:
keśareṣvaṅgapūjā syātpatreṣu ca tator'cayet /
rāmabhakto mahātejāḥ kapirājo mahābalaḥ //
1.74.d:
केशरेष्वङ्गपूजा स्यात्पत्रेषु च ततोर्ऽचयेत् ।
रामभक्तो महातेजाः कपिराजो महाबलः ॥
1.74.m: the worship of the limbs should be upon the filaments; and then on the petals one should worship: / the devotee of Rāma, the greatly radiant, the king of monkeys, the exceedingly powerful,

1.74.s:
droṇādrihārako merupīṭhakārcanakārakaḥ /
dakṣiṇāśābhāskaraśca sarvavighnavināśakaḥ //
1.74.d:
द्रोणाद्रिहारको मेरुपीठकार्चनकारकः ।
दक्षिणाशाभास्करश्च सर्वविघ्नविनाशकः ॥
1.74.m: the bringer of Mount Droṇa, the worshipper of the ritual seat of Meru, / the sun of the southern quarter, and the destroyer of all obstacles.

1.74.s:
itthaṃ sampūjya nāmāni dalāgreṣu tator'cayet /
sugrīvamaṅgada nīlaṃ jāṃbavantaṃ nalaṃ tathā //
1.74.d:
इत्थं सम्पूज्य नामानि दलाग्रेषु ततोर्ऽचयेत् ।
सुग्रीवमङ्गद नीलं जांबवन्तं नलं तथा ॥
1.74.m: Having worshipped these names in this way, one should then worship on the tips of the petals: / Sugrīva, Aṅgada, Nīla, Jāmbavat, and Nala,

1.74.s:
suṣeṇaṃ dvividaṃ maindaṃ lokapālastator'cayet /
vajrādyānapi saṃpūjya siddhaścaivaṃ manurbhavet //
1.74.d:
सुषेणं द्विविदं मैन्दं लोकपालस्ततोर्ऽचयेत् ।
वज्राद्यानपि संपूज्य सिद्धश्चैवं मनुर्भवेत् ॥
1.74.m: Suṣeṇa, Dvivida, and Mainda; then one should worship the guardians of the world. / Having also worshipped the thunderbolt and the other [weapons], the mantra becomes perfected.

1.74.s:
mantraṃ navaśataṃ rātrau japeddaśadināvadhi /
yo narastasya naśyanti rājaśatrūtthabhītayaḥ //
1.74.d:
मन्त्रं नवशतं रात्रौ जपेद्दशदिनावधि ।
यो नरस्तस्य नश्यन्ति राजशत्रूत्थभीतयः ॥
1.74.m: A man who recites the mantra nine hundred [times] at night for a period of ten days, / his fears arising from kings and enemies are destroyed.

1.74.s:
mātuliṅgāmrakadalīphalairhutvā sahasrakam /
dvāviṃśatibrahmacāri viprānsaṃbhojayecchucīn //
1.74.d:
मातुलिङ्गाम्रकदलीफलैर्हुत्वा सहस्रकम् ।
द्वाविंशतिब्रह्मचारि विप्रान्संभोजयेच्छुचीन् ॥
1.74.m: Offering a thousand oblations into the fire with citron, mango, and plantain fruits, / one should feed twenty-two pure celibate brahmins.

1.74.s:
evaṅkṛte bhūtaviṣagraharogādyupadravāḥ /
naśyanti tatkṣaṇādeva vidveṣigrahadānavāḥ //
1.74.d:
एवङ्कृते भूतविषग्रहरोगाद्युपद्रवाः ।
नश्यन्ति तत्क्षणादेव विद्वेषिग्रहदानवाः ॥
1.74.m: When this is done, afflictions such as spirits, poisons, seizing planets, and diseases, / and hostile seizing planets and dānavas, are destroyed in that very instant.

1.74.s:
aṣṭottaraśatenāṃbu mantritaṃ viṣanāśanam /
bhūtāpasmārakṛtyotthajvare tanmantramantritaiḥ //
1.74.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतेनांबु मन्त्रितं विषनाशनम् ।
भूतापस्मारकृत्योत्थज्वरे तन्मन्त्रमन्त्रितैः ॥
1.74.m: Water consecrated with one hundred and eight [recitations] destroys poison. / In a fever arising from spirits, epilepsy, or black magic, with ashes

1.74.s:
bhasmabhiḥ salilairvāpi tāḍayejjvariṇaṃ krudhā /
tridinājjvaramukto 'sau sukhaṃ ca labhate naraḥ //
1.74.d:
भस्मभिः सलिलैर्वापि ताडयेज्ज्वरिणं क्रुधा ।
त्रिदिनाज्ज्वरमुक्तो ऽसौ सुखं च लभते नरः ॥
1.74.m: or water consecrated with that mantra, one should strike the feverish person in anger; / after three days, that man is freed from the fever and attains comfort.

1.74.s:
auṣadhaṃ vā jalaṃ vāpi bhuktvā tanmantramantritam /
sarvānrogānparābhūya sukhī bhavati tatkṣaṇāt //
1.74.d:
औषधं वा जलं वापि भुक्त्वा तन्मन्त्रमन्त्रितम् ।
सर्वान्रोगान्पराभूय सुखी भवति तत्क्षणात् ॥
1.74.m: Having consumed medicine or water consecrated with that mantra, / having overcome all diseases, he becomes happy at that very moment.

1.74.s:
tajjaptabhasmaliptāṅgo bhuktvā tanmantritaṃ payaḥ /
yoddhuṃ gacchecca yo mantrī śastrasaṃghairṃna bādhyate //
1.74.d:
तज्जप्तभस्मलिप्ताङ्गो भुक्त्वा तन्मन्त्रितं पयः ।
योद्धुं गच्छेच्च यो मन्त्री शस्त्रसंघैर्ंन बाध्यते ॥
1.74.m: A practitioner who goes to fight with his body smeared with ashes over which that was recited, and having drunk water consecrated with it, / is not harmed by hosts of weapons.

1.74.s:
śaskṣataṃ vraṇasphoṭo lūtāsphoṭo 'pi bhasmanā /
trirjaptena ca saṃspṛṣṭāḥ śuṣyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.74.d:
शस्क्षतं व्रणस्फोटो लूतास्फोटो ऽपि भस्मना ।
त्रिर्जप्तेन च संस्पृष्टाः शुष्यन्त्येव न संशयः ॥
1.74.m: A weapon wound, an ulcer boil, or a spider boil, touched with ash / recited over three times, will certainly dry up, there is no doubt.

1.74.s:
japedarkāstamārabhya yāvadarkedayo bhavet /
mantraṃ saptadinaṃ yāvañcādāya bhasmakīlakau //
1.74.d:
जपेदर्कास्तमारभ्य यावदर्केदयो भवेत् ।
मन्त्रं सप्तदिनं यावञ्चादाय भस्मकीलकौ ॥
1.74.m: Starting from sunset until sunrise, / he should recite the mantra for seven days; and taking two wooden pegs with ash,

1.74.s:
nikhanedabhimantryāśuśatrūṇāṃ dvāryalakṣitaḥ /
vidveṣaṃ mitha āpannāḥ palāyante 'rayo 'cirāt //
1.74.d:
निखनेदभिमन्त्र्याशुशत्रूणां द्वार्यलक्षितः ।
विद्वेषं मिथ आपन्नाः पलायन्ते ऽरयो ऽचिरात् ॥
1.74.m: having quickly consecrated them, he should bury them unseen at the door of the enemies; / having fallen into mutual enmity, the enemies flee before long.

1.74.s:
bhasmāṃbu candanaṃ mantrī mantreṇānena mantritam /
bhakṣyādiyojitaṃ yasmai dadāti sa tu dāsavat //
1.74.d:
भस्मांबु चन्दनं मन्त्री मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितम् ।
भक्ष्यादियोजितं यस्मै ददाति स तु दासवत् ॥
1.74.m: The practitioner gives ash, water, or sandalwood paste consecrated with this mantra, / mixed with food and the like, to whomever, that person becomes like a slave;

1.74.s:
krūrāśca jantavo 'pyevaṃ bhavanti vaśavartinaḥ /
gṛhītveśanadiskaṃsthaṃ karañjatarumūlakam //
1.74.d:
क्रूराश्च जन्तवो ऽप्येवं भवन्ति वशवर्तिनः ।
गृहीत्वेशनदिस्कंस्थं करञ्जतरुमूलकम् ॥
1.74.m: even cruel beasts become obedient in this way. / Taking the root of a karañja tree situated in the north-eastern direction,

1.74.s:
kṛtvā tenāṅguṣṭamātrāṃ pratimāṃ ca hanūmataḥ /
kṛtvā prāṇapratiṣṭāṃ ca siṃdūrādyaiḥ prapūjya ca //
1.74.d:
कृत्वा तेनाङ्गुष्टमात्रां प्रतिमां च हनूमतः ।
कृत्वा प्राणप्रतिष्टां च सिंदूराद्यैः प्रपूज्य च ॥
1.74.m: and having fashioned from it an image of Hanumān the size of a thumb, / and having performed the installation of life-breath and worshipped it with vermilion and other offerings,

1.74.s:
gṛhasyābhimukhī dvāre nikhanenmantramuñcaran /
grahābhicārarogāgniviṣacauranṛpodbhavāḥ //
1.74.d:
गृहस्याभिमुखी द्वारे निखनेन्मन्त्रमुञ्चरन् ।
ग्रहाभिचाररोगाग्निविषचौरनृपोद्भवाः ॥
1.74.m: he should bury it facing the house at the door, uttering the mantra. / Afflictions arising from seizing planets, sorcery, disease, fire, poison, thieves, and kings

1.74.s:
na jāyante gṛhe tasmin kadācidapyupadravāḥ /
tadgṛhaṃ dhanaputrādyairedhate pratyahaṃ ciram //
1.74.d:
न जायन्ते गृहे तस्मिन् कदाचिदप्युपद्रवाः ।
तद्गृहं धनपुत्राद्यैरेधते प्रत्यहं चिरम् ॥
1.74.m: never arise in that house at any time; / that house prospers daily for a long time with wealth, sons, and the like.

1.74.s:
niśi yatra vane bhasma mṛtsnayā vāpi yatnataḥ /
śatroḥ pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvā hṛdi nāma samālikhet //
1.74.d:
निशि यत्र वने भस्म मृत्स्नया वापि यत्नतः ।
शत्रोः प्रतिकृतिं कृत्वा हृदि नाम समालिखेत् ॥
1.74.m: At night, wherever in the forest, having carefully made an effigy of the enemy / with ash or clay, he should write the name upon the chest.

1.74.s:
kṛtvā prāṇapratiṣṭāntaṃ bhindyācchastrairmanuṃ japan /
mantrānte proñcarecchatrornāma chindhi ca bhindhi ca //
1.74.d:
कृत्वा प्राणप्रतिष्टान्तं भिन्द्याच्छस्त्रैर्मनुं जपन् ।
मन्त्रान्ते प्रोञ्चरेच्छत्रोर्नाम छिन्धि च भिन्धि च ॥
1.74.m: Having performed up to the installation of life-breath, reciting the mantra, he should pierce it with weapons; / at the end of the mantra, he should utter the enemy’s name and: ‘Cut and pierce!’

1.74.s:
mārayeti ca tasyānte dantairoṣṭaṃ nipūḍya ca /
pāṇyostale prapīḍyātha tyaktvā taṃ svagṛhaṃ vrajet //
1.74.d:
मारयेति च तस्यान्ते दन्तैरोष्टं निपूड्य च ।
पाण्योस्तले प्रपीड्याथ त्यक्त्वा तं स्वगृहं व्रजेत् ॥
1.74.m: And at its end, [pronouncing] “Kill!”, biting the lip with the teeth / and pressing the palms of the hands together, he should leave it and go to his own house.

1.74.s:
kurvansaptadinaṃ caivaṃ hanyācchatruṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
rājikālavaṇairmuktacikuraḥ pitṛkānane //
1.74.d:
कुर्वन्सप्तदिनं चैवं हन्याच्छत्रुं न संशयः ।
राजिकालवणैर्मुक्तचिकुरः पितृकानने ॥
1.74.m: Doing this for seven days, he slays his enemy without doubt. / With disheveled hair in the cemetery, with black mustard and salt,

1.74.s:
dhattūraphalapuṣpaiśca nakharomaviṣairapi /
dvika(kāka)kauśikagṛdhrāṇāṃ pakṣaiḥ śleṣmāntakākṣajaiḥ //
1.74.d:
धत्तूरफलपुष्पैश्च नखरोमविषैरपि ।
द्विक(काक)कौशिकगृध्राणां पक्षैः श्लेष्मान्तकाक्षजैः ॥
1.74.m: with dhattūra fruits and flowers, and with nails, hair, and poisons, / with feathers of crows, owls, and vultures, and with the kindling-sticks

1.74.s:
samiddhistriśataṃ yāmayadiṅmukho juhuyānniśi /
evaṃ saptadinaṃ kurvanmārayeduddhataṃ ripun //
1.74.d:
समिद्धिस्त्रिशतं यामयदिङ्मुखो जुहुयान्निशि ।
एवं सप्तदिनं कुर्वन्मारयेदुद्धतं रिपुन् ॥
1.74.m: produced from the śleṣmāntaka [and] akṣa trees, facing the southern quarter, he should offer three hundred oblations at night. / Doing this for seven days, he causes his haughty enemy to be killed.

1.74.s:
vitrāsastridinaṃ rātrau śmaśāne ṣaṭśataṃ japet /
tato vetāla utthāya vadedbhāvi śubhāśubham //
1.74.d:
वित्रासस्त्रिदिनं रात्रौ श्मशाने षट्शतं जपेत् ।
ततो वेताल उत्थाय वदेद्भावि शुभाशुभम् ॥
1.74.m: Free of fear, he should recite [the mantra] six hundred times at night in the cremation ground for three days. / Then a vetāla, rising up, will speak of the future good and evil.

1.74.s:
kiṅkarībhūya vartteta kurute sādhakoditam /
bhāsmāṃbumantritaṃ rātrau sahasrāvṛttikaṃ punaḥ //
1.74.d:
किङ्करीभूय वर्त्तेत कुरुते साधकोदितम् ।
भास्मांबुमन्त्रितं रात्रौ सहस्रावृत्तिकं पुनः ॥
1.74.m: Becoming his servant, he remains and does whatever the practitioner commands. / Again, water consecrated with ashes, recited over a thousand times at night,

1.74.s:
dinatrayaṃ ca tatpaścātprakṣipetpratimāsu ca /
yāsu kāsu ca sthūlāsu laghuṣvapi viśeṣataḥ //
1.74.d:
दिनत्रयं च तत्पश्चात्प्रक्षिपेत्प्रतिमासु च ।
यासु कासु च स्थूलासु लघुष्वपि विशेषतः ॥
1.74.m: and after three days cast upon images— / upon any images whatsoever, whether large or especially small—

1.74.s:
mantraprabhāvāñcalanaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
aṣṭamyāṃ vā caturdaśyāṃ kuje vā ravivāsare //
1.74.d:
मन्त्रप्रभावाञ्चलनं भवत्येव न संशयः ।
अष्टम्यां वा चतुर्दश्यां कुजे वा रविवासरे ॥
1.74.m: movement definitely occurs by the power of the mantra, without doubt. / On the eighth or fourteenth lunar day, or on a Tuesday or Sunday,

1.74.s:
hanumatpratimāṃ paṭṭe māṣaiḥ snehapariplutaiḥ /
kuryādramyāṃ viśuddhātmā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitām //
1.74.d:
हनुमत्प्रतिमां पट्टे माषैः स्नेहपरिप्लुतैः ।
कुर्याद्रम्यां विशुद्धात्मा सर्वलक्षणलक्षिताम् ॥
1.74.m: the pure-minded practitioner should make a charming image of Hanumat on a board out of māṣa beans drenched in oil, / endowed with all auspicious marks.

1.74.s:
tailadīpaṃ vāmabhāge ghṛtadīpaṃ tu dakṣiṇe /
saṃsthāpyāvāhayetpaścānmūlamantreṇa mantravit //
1.74.d:
तैलदीपं वामभागे घृतदीपं तु दक्षिणे ।
संस्थाप्यावाहयेत्पश्चान्मूलमन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.74.m: Placing an oil lamp on the left side and a ghee lamp on the right side, / the knower of mantras should then invoke [him] using the root-mantra.

1.74.s:
prāṇapratiṣṭāṃ kṛtvā ca pādyādīni samarpayet /
raktacandanapuṣpaiśca siṃdūrādyaiḥ samarcayet //
1.74.d:
प्राणप्रतिष्टां कृत्वा च पाद्यादीनि समर्पयेत् ।
रक्तचन्दनपुष्पैश्च सिंदूराद्यैः समर्चयेत् ॥
1.74.m: Having performed the establishment of the breath of life, he should offer water for the feet and other rites, / and worship him with red sandalwood, flowers, vermilion, and so forth.

1.74.s:
dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ pradāyātha naivedyaṃ ca samarpayet /
apūpamodanaṃ śākamodakānvaṭakādikam //
1.74.d:
धूपं दीपं प्रदायाथ नैवेद्यं च समर्पयेत् ।
अपूपमोदनं शाकमोदकान्वटकादिकम् ॥
1.74.m: Offering incense and a lamp, he should then present the food offering: / sweet cakes, cooked rice, vegetables, sweet dumplings, savory fried cakes, and the like.

1.74.s:
sājyaṃ ca tatsamarpyātha mūlamantreṇa mantravit /
akhaṇḍitānyahilatādalāni saptaviṃśatim //
1.74.d:
साज्यं च तत्समर्प्याथ मूलमन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ।
अखण्डितान्यहिलतादलानि सप्तविंशतिम् ॥
1.74.m: Having offered that along with ghee using the root-mantra, the knower of mantras / should take twenty-seven unbroken betel leaves,

1.74.s:
tridhā kṛtvā sapūgāni mūlenaiva samarpayet /
evaṃ saṃpūjya mantrajño japeddaśaśanta manum //
1.74.d:
त्रिधा कृत्वा सपूगानि मूलेनैव समर्पयेत् ।
एवं संपूज्य मन्त्रज्ञो जपेद्दशशन्त मनुम् ॥
1.74.m: divide them threefold, and offer them along with betel nuts using the root-mantra alone. / Having worshipped thus, the knower of mantras should recite the mantra one thousand times.

1.74.s:
karpūrārārtikaṃ kṛtvā stutvā ca bahudhā sudhīḥ /
nijepsitaṃ nivedyātha vidhivadvisṛjettataḥ //
1.74.d:
कर्पूरारार्तिकं कृत्वा स्तुत्वा च बहुधा सुधीः ।
निजेप्सितं निवेद्याथ विधिवद्विसृजेत्ततः ॥
1.74.m: Performing the wave-offering with camphor and praising him in many ways, the wise man, / having communicated his own desire, should then dismiss him according to rule.

1.74.s:
naivedyānnena saṃbhojya brāhmaṇānsaptasaṃkhyayā /
niveditāni parṇāni tebhyo dadyādvibhajya ca //
1.74.d:
नैवेद्यान्नेन संभोज्य ब्राह्मणान्सप्तसंख्यया ।
निवेदितानि पर्णानि तेभ्यो दद्याद्विभज्य च ॥
1.74.m: Feeding seven brāhmaṇas with the consecrated food offerings, / he should distribute and give them the leaves that were offered.

1.74.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathā śakti dattvā tān visṛjetsudhīḥ /
tata iṣṭagaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.74.d:
दक्षिणां च यथा शक्ति दत्त्वा तान् विसृजेत्सुधीः ।
तत इष्टगणैः सार्द्धं स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.74.m: Giving a priestly fee according to his ability, the wise man should dismiss them. / Then, remaining silent, he should eat himself together with his loved ones.

1.74.s:
taddine bhūmiśayyāṃ ca brahmacaryyaṃ samācaret /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute martyaḥ so 'cirādeva niścitam //
1.74.d:
तद्दिने भूमिशय्यां च ब्रह्मचर्य्यं समाचरेत् ।
एवं यः कुरुते मर्त्यः सो ऽचिरादेव निश्चितम् ॥
1.74.m: On that day he should sleep on the bare ground and observe celibacy. / The mortal who acts thus, surely and before long,

1.74.s:
prāpnuyātsakalānkāmānkapīśasya prasādataḥ /
hanumatpratimāṃ bhūmau vilikhettatpuro manum //
1.74.d:
प्राप्नुयात्सकलान्कामान्कपीशस्य प्रसादतः ।
हनुमत्प्रतिमां भूमौ विलिखेत्तत्पुरो मनुम् ॥
1.74.m: will obtain all desires through the grace of the lord of monkeys. / He should draw an image of Hanumat on the ground, and in front of it the mantra:

1.74.s:
sādhyanāma dvitīyāntaṃ vimocaya vimocaya /
tatpūrvaṃ mārjayedvāmapāṇinātha punarlikhet /
evamaṣṭottaraśataṃ likhitvā mārjayetpunaḥ //
1.74.d:
साध्यनाम द्वितीयान्तं विमोचय विमोचय ।
तत्पूर्वं मार्जयेद्वामपाणिनाथ पुनर्लिखेत् ।
एवमष्टोत्तरशतं लिखित्वा मार्जयेत्पुनः ॥
1.74.m: The name of the target in the accusative case, followed by: “Release, release!” / He should wipe it clean with his left hand and then write it again; / having written it thus one hundred and eight times, he should wipe it again.

1.74.s:
evaṃ kṛte mahākārāgṛhācchīghraṃ vimucyate /
evamanyāni karmāṇi kuryyāntpallavamullikhan //
1.74.d:
एवं कृते महाकारागृहाच्छीघ्रं विमुच्यते ।
एवमन्यानि कर्माणि कुर्य्यान्त्पल्लवमुल्लिखन् ॥
1.74.m: When this is done, one is swiftly freed from a great prison. / Thus one should perform other ritual acts, writing the appended phrases.

1.74.s:
sarṣapairvaśyakṛddhomo vidveṣe hayamārajaiḥ /
kuṅkumairidhmakāṣṭhairvā marīcairjīrakairapi //
1.74.d:
सर्षपैर्वश्यकृद्धोमो विद्वेषे हयमारजैः ।
कुङ्कुमैरिध्मकाष्ठैर्वा मरीचैर्जीरकैरपि ॥
1.74.m: Oblation with mustard seeds brings subjugation; in causing enmity, with parts of the oleander, / with saffron, firewood, or black pepper and cumin.

1.74.s:
jvare dūrvāguḍūcībhirdadhnā kṣīreṇa vā ghṛtaiḥ /
śūle karañjavātārisamidbhistailalolitaiḥ //
1.74.d:
ज्वरे दूर्वागुडूचीभिर्दध्ना क्षीरेण वा घृतैः ।
शूले करञ्जवातारिसमिद्भिस्तैललोलितैः ॥
1.74.m: In fever, with dūrvā grass, guḍūcī, curd, milk, or ghee; / in piercing pain, with kindling-sticks of the karañja and castor plant smeared with oil,

1.74.s:
tailāktābhiśca nirguṇḍīsamidbhirvā prayatnataḥ /
saubhāgye candanaiścendralocanairvā lavaṅgakaiḥ //
1.74.d:
तैलाक्ताभिश्च निर्गुण्डीसमिद्भिर्वा प्रयत्नतः ।
सौभाग्ये चन्दनैश्चेन्द्रलोचनैर्वा लवङ्गकैः ॥
1.74.m: or with kindling-sticks of nirguṇḍī anointed with oil, carefully [offered]; / for good fortune, with sandalwood, indralocana, or cloves;

1.74.s:
sugandhapuṣpairvastrāptyai tattaddhānyaistadāptaye /
ripupādarajobhiśca rājīlavaṇamiśritaiḥ //
1.74.d:
सुगन्धपुष्पैर्वस्त्राप्त्यै तत्तद्धान्यैस्तदाप्तये ।
रिपुपादरजोभिश्च राजीलवणमिश्रितैः ॥
1.74.m: for obtaining garments, with fragrant flowers; for gaining various grains, with those respective grains; / and with dust from an enemy’s feet mixed with black mustard and salt,

1.74.s:
homayetsaptarātraṃ ca ripuryāti yamālayam /
dhānyaiḥ saṃprāpyate dhānyamannairannasamucchrayaḥ //
1.74.d:
होमयेत्सप्तरात्रं च रिपुर्याति यमालयम् ।
धान्यैः संप्राप्यते धान्यमन्नैरन्नसमुच्छ्रयः ॥
1.74.m: he should offer oblations for seven nights, and the enemy goes to the abode of Yama. / By grains, grain is obtained; by food, an abundance of food;

1.74.s:
tilājyakṣīramadhubhirmahiṣīgosamṛddhaye /
kiṃ bahūktairviṣe vyādhau śāntau mohe ca māraṇe //
1.74.d:
तिलाज्यक्षीरमधुभिर्महिषीगोसमृद्धये ।
किं बहूक्तैर्विषे व्याधौ शान्तौ मोहे च मारणे ॥
1.74.m: with sesamum, ghee, milk, and honey, for the prosperity of buffaloes and cows. / What need of saying much? In cases of poison, disease, pacification, delusion, and killing;

1.74.s:
vivāde staṃbhane dyūte bhūtabhītau ca saṃkaṭe /
vaśye yuddhe kṣate divye bandhamokṣe mahāvane //
1.74.d:
विवादे स्तंभने द्यूते भूतभीतौ च संकटे ।
वश्ये युद्धे क्षते दिव्ये बन्धमोक्षे महावने ॥
1.74.m: in dispute, immobilization, gambling, fear of spirits, and peril; / in subjugation, battle, wounds, ordeals, liberation from bonds, and in the great forest,

1.74.s:
sādhito 'yaṃ nṛṇāṃ dadyānmantraḥ śreyaḥ suniścitam /
vakṣye 'tha hanumadyantraṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam //
1.74.d:
साधितो ऽयं नृणां दद्यान्मन्त्रः श्रेयः सुनिश्चितम् ।
वक्ष्ये ऽथ हनुमद्यन्त्रं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् ॥
1.74.m: this mantra, when mastered, will assuredly grant the highest good to men. / I shall now declare the yantra of Hanumat, which grants all accomplishments.

1.74.s:
lāṅgūlākārasaṃyuktaṃ valayatritayaṃ likhet /
sādhyanāma likhenmadhye pāśibīja praveṣṭitam //
1.74.d:
लाङ्गूलाकारसंयुक्तं वलयत्रितयं लिखेत् ।
साध्यनाम लिखेन्मध्ये पाशिबीज प्रवेष्टितम् ॥
1.74.m: One should draw three concentric circles provided with the form of a tail. / In the middle he should write the name of the target, encircled by the bīja of the noose-bearer.

1.74.s:
uparyaṣṭacchadaṃ kṛtvā patreṣu kavacaṃ likhet /
tadbahirdaṃhamālikhya tadbahiścaturasrakam //
1.74.d:
उपर्यष्टच्छदं कृत्वा पत्रेषु कवचं लिखेत् ।
तद्बहिर्दंहमालिख्य तद्बहिश्चतुरस्रकम् ॥
1.74.m: Above it, having made an eight-petalled lotus, he should write the armor-mantra on the petals. / Outside that, having drawn a [...] circle, outside that a square.

1.74.s:
caturasasrasya rekhāgre triśūlāni samālikhet /
saiṃ bījaṃ bhūpurasyāṣṭavajreṣu vilikhettataḥ //
1.74.d:
चतुरसस्रस्य रेखाग्रे त्रिशूलानि समालिखेत् ।
सैं बीजं भूपुरस्याष्टवज्रेषु विलिखेत्ततः ॥
1.74.m: At the tips of the lines of the square he should draw tridents. / Then he should write the bīja 'saiṃ' on the eight thunderbolts of the earth-city.

1.74.s:
koṇeṣvakuṃśamālikhya mālāmantreṇa veṣṭayet /
tatsarvaṃ veṣṭayedyantravalayatritayena ca //
1.74.d:
कोणेष्वकुंशमालिख्य मालामन्त्रेण वेष्टयेत् ।
तत्सर्वं वेष्टयेद्यन्त्रवलयत्रितयेन च ॥
1.74.m: Having written the goad in the corners, he should surround it with the mālā-mantra. / He should enclose all that with three circles of the yantra.

1.74.s:
śilāyāṃ phalake vastre tāmrapatre 'tha kuḍyake /
tāḍapatre 'tha bhūrje vā rocanānābhikuṅkubhaiḥ //
1.74.d:
शिलायां फलके वस्त्रे ताम्रपत्रे ऽथ कुड्यके ।
ताडपत्रे ऽथ भूर्जे वा रोचनानाभिकुङ्कुभैः ॥
1.74.m: On a stone, a wooden board, cloth, a copper sheet, or a wall, / on a palm-leaf or birch bark, with yellow pigment, musk, and saffron,

1.74.s:
yantrametatsamālikhya nirāhāro jitendriyaḥ /
kapeḥ prāṇānpratiṣṭāpya pūjayettadyathāvidhi //
1.74.d:
यन्त्रमेतत्समालिख्य निराहारो जितेन्द्रियः ।
कपेः प्राणान्प्रतिष्टाप्य पूजयेत्तद्यथाविधि ॥
1.74.m: having drawn this yantra, fasting and with senses subdued, / having established the vital breath of the monkey, he should worship it according to rule.

1.74.s:
aśeṣaduḥkhaśāntyarthaḥ yantraṃ saṃdhārayed budhaḥ /
mārījvarābhicārādisarvopadravanāśanam //
1.74.d:
अशेषदुःखशान्त्यर्थः यन्त्रं संधारयेद् बुधः ।
मारीज्वराभिचारादिसर्वोपद्रवनाशनम् ॥
1.74.m: For the pacification of endless suffering, the wise man should wear the yantra, / which destroys all afflictions such as pestilence, fevers, and malevolent sorcery.

1.74.s:
yoṣitāmapi bālānāṃ dhṛtaṃ janamanoharam /
bhūtakṛtyāpiśācānāṃ darśanādeva nāśanam //
1.74.d:
योषितामपि बालानां धृतं जनमनोहरम् ।
भूतकृत्यापिशाचानां दर्शनादेव नाशनम् ॥
1.74.m: Worn by women and children, it captivates the minds of people; / it destroys bhūtas, kṛtyās, and piśācas by its very sight.

1.74.s:
mālāmantramatho vakṣye tāro vāgviṣṇugehinī /
dīrghatrayānvitā māyā prāguktaṃ kūṭapañcakam //
1.74.d:
मालामन्त्रमथो वक्ष्ये तारो वाग्विष्णुगेहिनी ।
दीर्घत्रयान्विता माया प्रागुक्तं कूटपञ्चकम् ॥
1.74.m: Now I shall declare the mālā-mantra: the praṇava, Sarasvatī, the consort of Viṣṇu, / the māyā-bīja endowed with three long vowels, the five-fold combination previously spoken,

1.74.s:
dhruvo hṛddhanumānṅeṃto 'tha prakaṭaparākramaḥ /
ākrāntadigmaṇḍalānte yaśovitānasaṃvadet //
1.74.d:
ध्रुवो हृद्धनुमान्ङेंतो ऽथ प्रकटपराक्रमः ।
आक्रान्तदिग्मण्डलान्ते यशोवितानसंवदेत् ॥
1.74.m: the dhruva, the heart, 'Hanumat' in the dative case, and then: 'O you of manifest valor!', / at the end of 'who have pervaded the circle of the quarters', one should say: 'whose canopy of fame

1.74.s:
dhavalīkṛtavarṇānte jagattritayavajra ca /
dehajvaladagnisūrya koṭyante ca samaprabha //
1.74.d:
धवलीकृतवर्णान्ते जगत्त्रितयवज्र च ।
देहज्वलदग्निसूर्य कोट्यन्ते च समप्रभ ॥
1.74.m: has whitened the three worlds', and 'O adamantine / body, whose splendor is equal to crores of blazing fires and suns!',

1.74.s:
tanūruhapadānte tu rudrāvatāra saṃvadet /
laṅkāpurī tataḥ paścāddahanodadhilaṅghana //
1.74.d:
तनूरुहपदान्ते तु रुद्रावतार संवदेत् ।
लङ्कापुरी ततः पश्चाद्दहनोदधिलङ्घन ॥
1.74.m: and after the word 'whose body hair...', one should say: 'O incarnation of Rudra!', / then 'the city of Laṅkā', 'O burner of...', 'who leaped over the ocean!',

1.74.s:
daśagrīvaśiraḥ paścātkṛtāntakapadaṃ vadet /
sītānte śvasanapadaṃ vāyvante sutamīrayet //
1.74.d:
दशग्रीवशिरः पश्चात्कृतान्तकपदं वदेत् ।
सीतान्ते श्वसनपदं वाय्वन्ते सुतमीरयेत् ॥
1.74.m: after 'the heads of the ten-necked one', one should say the word 'death-dealer', / after 'Sītā', the word 'breath-giving', and after 'wind', one should utter 'son!',

1.74.s:
añjanāgarbhasaṃbhūtaḥ śrīrāmalakṣmaṇānvitaḥ /
nandanti kara varṇānte sainyaprākāra īrayet //
1.74.d:
अञ्जनागर्भसंभूतः श्रीरामलक्ष्मणान्वितः ।
नन्दन्ति कर वर्णान्ते सैन्यप्राकार ईरयेत् ॥
1.74.m: ‘born from the womb of Añjanā’, ‘accompanied by the blessed Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa’, / after the syllable that causes delight, one should utter ‘rampart of the army!’,

1.74.s:
sugrīvasakhyakādūrṇādraṇavālinivarhaṇa /
kāraṇadroṇaśabdānte parvatotpāṭaneti ca //
1.74.d:
सुग्रीवसख्यकादूर्णाद्रणवालिनिवर्हण ।
कारणद्रोणशब्दान्ते पर्वतोत्पाटनेति च ॥
1.74.m: ‘who eagerly forged friendship with Sugrīva’, ‘destroyer of Vālin in battle’, / after the words ‘the cause of... Droṇa’, one should say ‘uprooter of the mountain!’,

1.74.s:
aśokavanavīthyante dāruṇākṣakumāraka /
chedanānte vanarakṣākarānte tu samūha ca //
1.74.d:
अशोकवनवीथ्यन्ते दारुणाक्षकुमारक ।
छेदनान्ते वनरक्षाकरान्ते तु समूह च ॥
1.74.m: after ‘avenue of the Aśoka grove’, ‘severer of the fierce prince Akṣa’, / after ‘severing’, and after ‘protecting the grove’, ‘the host

1.74.s:
vibhañjanānte brahmāstrabrahmaśakti graseti ca /
lakṣmaṇānte śaktibhedanivāraṇapadaṃ vadet //
1.74.d:
विभञ्जनान्ते ब्रह्मास्त्रब्रह्मशक्ति ग्रसेति च ।
लक्ष्मणान्ते शक्तिभेदनिवारणपदं वदेत् ॥
1.74.m: destroying’, and after ‘destroying’, ‘devourer of the Brahmā-missile and the Brahma-potency!’, / after ‘Lakṣmaṇa’, one should speak the phrase ‘averter of the piercing by the spear!’,

1.74.s:
viśalyoṣadhiśabdānte samānayana saṃpaṭhet /
bālodita tato bhānumaṇḍalagrasaneti ca //
1.74.d:
विशल्योषधिशब्दान्ते समानयन संपठेत् ।
बालोदित ततो भानुमण्डलग्रसनेति च ॥
1.74.m: after the word ‘herb that removes arrows’, one should recite ‘bringer of!’, / then ‘who swallowed the disc of the newly risen sun!’,

1.74.s:
meghanādahomapadādvidhvaṃsanapadaṃ vadet /
indrajidūdhakārānte ṇasītāsakṣaketi ca //
1.74.d:
मेघनादहोमपदाद्विध्वंसनपदं वदेत् ।
इन्द्रजिदूधकारान्ते णसीतासक्षकेति च ॥
1.74.m: after the word ‘the sacrifice of Meghanāda’, one should say the word ‘destroyer of!’, / and after ‘slayer of Indrajit’, ‘cause of life to Sītā!’.

1.74.s:
rākṣasīsaṃghaśabdānte vidāraṇapadaṃ vadet /
kuṃbhakarṇādisaṃkīrtyavadhānte ca parāyaṇa //
1.74.d:
राक्षसीसंघशब्दान्ते विदारणपदं वदेत् ।
कुंभकर्णादिसंकीर्त्यवधान्ते च परायण ॥
1.74.m: After the word 'rākṣasī-saṃgha' ('host of demonesses'), one should utter the word 'vidāraṇa' ('rending'); / having mentioned Kumbhakarṇa and others, then 'parāyaṇa' ('wholly devoted to') after 'vadha' ('slaying'),

1.74.s:
śrīrāmabhaktivarṇānte tatpareti samudra ca /
vyomadrumalaṅghaneti mahāsāmarthya saṃvadet //
1.74.d:
श्रीरामभक्तिवर्णान्ते तत्परेति समुद्र च ।
व्योमद्रुमलङ्घनेति महासामर्थ्य संवदेत् ॥
1.74.m: and after the syllables 'śrī-rāma-bhakti' ('devotion to Śrī Rāma'), 'tatpara' ('intent upon that'); then 'samudra-' ('ocean-'), / 'vyoma-druma-laṅghana' ('leaping over the tree of the sky'), and one should utter 'mahā-sāmarthya' ('of great power');

1.74.s:
mahātejaḥpuñjaśabdādvirājamānavoñcaret /
svāmivacanasaṃpāditārjunānte ca saṃyuga //
1.74.d:
महातेजःपुञ्जशब्दाद्विराजमानवोञ्चरेत् ।
स्वामिवचनसंपादितार्जुनान्ते च संयुग ॥
1.74.m: after the word 'mahā-tejaḥ-puñja' ('mass of great splendor'), one should utter 'virājamāna' ('shining'); / then 'saṃyuga-' ('battle-') after 'arjuna', and 'svāmi-vacana-saṃpādita' ('accomplished through the lord's command');

1.74.s:
sahāyānte kumāreti brahmacārinpadaṃvadet /
gaṃbhīraśabdodayānte dakṣiṇāpatha saṃvadet /
mārttāṇḍameru śabdānte vadetparvatapīṭikā //
1.74.d:
सहायान्ते कुमारेति ब्रह्मचारिन्पदंवदेत् ।
गंभीरशब्दोदयान्ते दक्षिणापथ संवदेत् ।
मार्त्ताण्डमेरु शब्दान्ते वदेत्पर्वतपीटिका ॥
1.74.m: after 'sahāya' ('companion'), one should utter 'kumāra' ('youth') and the word 'brahmacārin' ('celibate student'); / after the rising of the word 'gambhīra' ('deep'), one should utter 'dakṣiṇāpatha' ('the southern region'); / after the words 'mārtāṇḍa-meru' ('sun and Meru'), one should utter 'parvata-pīṭhikā' ('mountain-pedestal');

1.74.s:
arcanānte tu sakalamantrānte mapadaṃ vadet /
ācāryamama śabdānte sarvagrahavināśana //
1.74.d:
अर्चनान्ते तु सकलमन्त्रान्ते मपदं वदेत् ।
आचार्यमम शब्दान्ते सर्वग्रहविनाशन ॥
1.74.m: after 'arcana' ('worship'), then 'sakala-mantra' ('all mantras'), at the end of which one should say the syllable 'ma'; / after the words 'ācārya mama' ('my preceptor'), then 'sarva-graha-vināśana' ('destroyer of all seize-spirits');

1.74.s:
sarvajvaroñcāṭanānte sarvaviṣavināśana /
sarvāpattinivāraṇa sarvaduṣṭanibarhaṇa //
1.74.d:
सर्वज्वरोञ्चाटनान्ते सर्वविषविनाशन ।
सर्वापत्तिनिवारण सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हण ॥
1.74.m: after 'sarva-jvaroccāṭana' ('expeller of all fevers'), 'sarva-viṣa-vināśana' ('destroyer of all poisons'), / 'sarvāpatti-nivāraṇa' ('averter of all misfortunes'), and 'sarva-duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa' ('subduer of all the wicked').

1.74.s: sarvavyādhyādi samprocya bhayānte ca nivāraṇa //
1.74.d: सर्वव्याध्यादि सम्प्रोच्य भयान्ते च निवारण ॥
1.74.m: Having spoken "all diseases and so forth," then after "fear" comes "dispeller";

1.74.s: sarvaśatrucchedaneti tato mama parasya ca //
1.74.d: सर्वशत्रुच्छेदनेति ततो मम परस्य च ॥
1.74.m: then "destroyer of all enemies"; next, "of me and of others";

1.74.s:
tatastribhuvanānte tu puṃstrīnapuṃsakātmakam /
sarvajīvapadānte tu jātaṃ vaśayayugmakam //
1.74.d:
ततस्त्रिभुवनान्ते तु पुंस्त्रीनपुंसकात्मकम् ।
सर्वजीवपदान्ते तु जातं वशययुग्मकम् ॥
1.74.m: then, after "the three worlds," "consisting of male, female, and neuter"; / and after the word "all living beings," the phrase "bring under control, bring under control";

1.74.s:
mamājñākārakaṃ paścātsaṃpādaya yugaṃ punaḥ /
tato nānānāmadheyānsarvān rājñaḥ sa saṃpaṭhet //
1.74.d:
ममाज्ञाकारकं पश्चात्संपादय युगं पुनः ।
ततो नानानामधेयान्सर्वान् राज्ञः स संपठेत् ॥
1.74.m: after that, "bring about, bring about obedience to my command"; / then he should recite all the kings along with their various names;

1.74.s:
parivārānmametyante sevakān kuru yugmakam /
sarvaśastravītyante ṣāṇi vidhvaṃsaya dvayam //
1.74.d:
परिवारान्ममेत्यन्ते सेवकान् कुरु युग्मकम् ।
सर्वशस्त्रवीत्यन्ते षाणि विध्वंसय द्वयम् ॥
1.74.m: at the end of "my retinue," "make servants, make servants"; / after "all weapons and missiles," "destroy, destroy the poisons";

1.74.s:
lajjādīrghatrayopetā hotrayaṃ caihi yugmakam /
vilomaṃ pañcakūṭāni sarvaśatrūnhanadvayam //
1.74.d:
लज्जादीर्घत्रयोपेता होत्रयं चैहि युग्मकम् ।
विलोमं पञ्चकूटानि सर्वशत्रून्हनद्वयम् ॥
1.74.m: [the syllable Hrīṃ] having the three long [vowels], three times "Ho", and twice "Ehi"; / in reverse order the five peak syllables; twice "slay all enemies";

1.74.s: parabalāni parānte sainyāni kṣobhayadvayam //
1.74.d: परबलानि परान्ते सैन्यानि क्षोभयद्वयम् ॥
1.74.m: after "the armies of enemies," twice "agitate the forces";

1.74.s: mama sarvaṃ kāryajātaṃ sādhayeti dvayaṃ tataḥ //
1.74.d: मम सर्वं कार्यजातं साधयेति द्वयं ततः ॥
1.74.m: then twice "accomplish all my undertakings";

1.74.s:
sarvaduṣṭadurjanānte mukhāni kīlayadvayam /
dhetrayaṃ varmatritayaṃ phaṭtrayaṃ hāntrayaṃ tataḥ //
1.74.d:
सर्वदुष्टदुर्जनान्ते मुखानि कीलयद्वयम् ।
धेत्रयं वर्मत्रितयं फट्त्रयं हान्त्रयं ततः ॥
1.74.m: after "all wicked and evil people," twice "pin their mouths"; / three times "Dhe", three armours [Hūṃ], three times "Phaṭ", and then three times "Hā";

1.74.s: vahnipriyānto mantro 'yaṃ mālāsaṃjño 'khileṣṭadaḥ //
1.74.d: वह्निप्रियान्तो मन्त्रो ऽयं मालासंज्ञो ऽखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.74.m: ending with the beloved of fire [Svāhā], this mantra named Mālā grants all desires.

1.74.s: vasvaṣṭabāṇavarṇo 'yaṃ mantraḥ sarveṣṭāsādhakaḥ //
1.74.d: वस्वष्टबाणवर्णो ऽयं मन्त्रः सर्वेष्टासाधकः ॥
1.74.m: This mantra of five hundred and eighty-eight syllables accomplishes all desires.

1.74.s:
mahābhaye mahotpāte smṛto 'yaṃ duḥkhanāśanaḥ /
dvādaśārṇasya ṣaṭkūṭaṃ tyaktvā bījaṃ tathādimam //
1.74.d:
महाभये महोत्पाते स्मृतो ऽयं दुःखनाशनः ।
द्वादशार्णस्य षट्कूटं त्यक्त्वा बीजं तथादिमम् ॥
1.74.m: Remembered in great fear and great calamity, it destroys suffering. / Having omitted the first seed-syllable and the six-peak [formula] of the twelve-syllabled [mantra],

1.74.s:
pañcakūṭātmako mantraḥ sarvakāmapradāyakaḥ /
rāmacandro muniścāsya gāyatrī chanda īritam //
1.74.d:
पञ्चकूटात्मको मन्त्रः सर्वकामप्रदायकः ।
रामचन्द्रो मुनिश्चास्य गायत्री छन्द ईरितम् ॥
1.74.m: the five-peak mantra is the bestower of all desires. / Rāmacandra is its seer, and the metre is declared to be gāyatrī;

1.74.s:
hanumāndevatā prokto viniyogo 'khilāptaye /
pañcabījaiḥ samastena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret //
1.74.d:
हनुमान्देवता प्रोक्तो विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ।
पञ्चबीजैः समस्तेन षडङ्गानि समाचरेत् ॥
1.74.m: Hanumān is proclaimed the deity, and the application is for the attainment of everything. / With the five seed-syllables together with the whole [mantra], one should perform the six limbs:

1.74.s:
rāmadūto lakṣmaṇānte prāṇadātāñjanīsutaḥ /
sītāśokavināśo 'yaṃ laṅkāprāsādabhañjanaḥ //
1.74.d:
रामदूतो लक्ष्मणान्ते प्राणदाताञ्जनीसुतः ।
सीताशोकविनाशो ऽयं लङ्काप्रासादभञ्जनः ॥
1.74.m: "Messenger of Rāma", "giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa", "son of Añjanī", / "destroyer of Sītā's sorrow", "shatterer of the palaces of Laṅkā" —

1.74.s:
hanumadādyāḥ pañcaite bījādyā ṅeyutāḥ punaḥ /
ṣaḍaṅgamanavo hyete dhyānapūjādi pūrvavat //
1.74.d:
हनुमदाद्याः पञ्चैते बीजाद्या ङेयुताः पुनः ।
षडङ्गमनवो ह्येते ध्यानपूजादि पूर्ववत् ॥
1.74.m: these five, beginning with Hanumān, preceded by the seed-syllables and ending with the dative case [Ṅe], / are indeed the mantras for the six limbs; meditation, worship, and the rest are as before.

1.74.s:
praṇavo vāgbhavaṃ padmā māyā dīrghatrayānvitā /
pañcakūṭāni mantro 'yaṃ rudrārṇaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ //
1.74.d:
प्रणवो वाग्भवं पद्मा माया दीर्घत्रयान्विता ।
पञ्चकूटानि मन्त्रो ऽयं रुद्रार्णः सर्वसिद्धिदः ॥
1.74.m: The Praṇava [Om], the seed of speech [Aiṃ], the lotus seed [Śrīṃ], and the seed of illusion [Hrīṃ] endowed with the three long vowels, / and the five-peak syllables: this eleven-syllabled mantra grants all spiritual attainments.

1.74.s:
dhyānapūjādikaṃ sarvamasyāpi pūrvavanmatam /
ayamārādhito mantraḥ sarvābhīṣṭapradāyakaḥ //
1.74.d:
ध्यानपूजादिकं सर्वमस्यापि पूर्ववन्मतम् ।
अयमाराधितो मन्त्रः सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायकः ॥
1.74.m: Its meditation, worship, and the rest are also considered to be entirely as before. / This mantra, when worshipped, bestows all desired things.

1.74.s:
namo bhagavate paścādanantaścandraśekharāṃ /
janeyāya mahānte tu balāyānte 'gnivallabhā //
1.74.d:
नमो भगवते पश्चादनन्तश्चन्द्रशेखरां ।
जनेयाय महान्ते तु बलायान्ते ऽग्निवल्लभा ॥
1.74.m: "Namo bhagavate", then Ananta [A], Candraśekhara with anusvāra [Aṃ], / "Janeyāya", then after "mahā" [comes] "balāya", and at the end the beloved of fire [Svāhā];

1.74.s:
aṣṭādaśārṇo mantro 'yaṃ sunirīśvarasaṃjñakaḥ /
chando 'nuṣṭupdevatā tu hanumānpavanātmajaḥ //
1.74.d:
अष्टादशार्णो मन्त्रो ऽयं सुनिरीश्वरसंज्ञकः ।
छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप्देवता तु हनुमान्पवनात्मजः ॥
1.74.m: this eighteen-syllabled mantra is known as Sunirīśvara. / The metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity is Hanumān, the son of the wind.

1.74.s:
haṃ bījaṃ vahnivanitā śaktiḥ proktā manīṣibhiḥ /
āñjaneyāya hṛdayaṃ śiraśca rudramūrtaye //
1.74.d:
हं बीजं वह्निवनिता शक्तिः प्रोक्ता मनीषिभिः ।
आञ्जनेयाय हृदयं शिरश्च रुद्रमूर्तये ॥
1.74.m: The seed-syllable is Haṃ, and the wife of fire [Svāhā] is declared by the wise to be the power. / "To the son of Añjanā" is the heart, "and to the Rudra-form" is the head;

1.74.s:
śikhāyāṃ vāyuputrāyāgnigarbhāya varmaṇi /
rāmadūtāya netraṃ syādbahyāstrāyāstramīritam //
1.74.d:
शिखायां वायुपुत्रायाग्निगर्भाय वर्मणि ।
रामदूताय नेत्रं स्याद्बह्यास्त्रायास्त्रमीरितम् ॥
1.74.m: "to the son of the wind" on the tuft, "to the fire-wombed" for the armor, / "to the messenger of Rāma" is the eye, and "to the external weapon" is declared the weapon.

1.74.s:
tatpacāmīkaranibhaṃ bhīghnasaṃvihitāñjalim /
calatkuṇḍaladīptāsyaṃ padmakṣaṃ mārutiṃ smaret //
1.74.d:
तत्पचामीकरनिभं भीघ्नसंविहिताञ्जलिम् ।
चलत्कुण्डलदीप्तास्यं पद्मक्षं मारुतिं स्मरेत् ॥
1.74.m: One should meditate on Māruti, resembling refined gold, with hands folded in reverent salutation, / his face radiant with swinging earrings, lotus-eyed.

1.74.s:
dhyātvaivamayutaṃ japtvā daśāṃśaṃ juhuyāttilaiḥ /
vaiṣṇave pūjayetpīṭhe prāguddiṣṭena vartmanā //
1.74.d:
ध्यात्वैवमयुतं जप्त्वा दशांशं जुहुयात्तिलैः ।
वैष्णवे पूजयेत्पीठे प्रागुद्दिष्टेन वर्त्मना ॥
1.74.m: Having meditated thus and recited [the mantra] ten thousand times, one should offer a tenth part in fire oblations with sesame seeds. / He should worship on a Vaiṣṇava seat in the manner previously described.

1.74.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ nityaṃ naktabhojī jitendriyaḥ /
japitvā kṣudrarogebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.74.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं नित्यं नक्तभोजी जितेन्द्रियः ।
जपित्वा क्षुद्ररोगेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.74.m: Reciting [it] one hundred and eight times daily, eating only at night, with senses restrained, / he is freed from petty ailments; of this there is no doubt.

1.74.s:
mahāroganivṛttyai tu sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ japet /
rākṣasaughaṃ vinighnantaṃ kapiṃ dhyātvādhanāśanam //
1.74.d:
महारोगनिवृत्त्यै तु सहस्रं प्रत्यहं जपेत् ।
राक्षसौघं विनिघ्नन्तं कपिं ध्यात्वाधनाशनम् ॥
1.74.m: For the removal of great diseases, one should recite [it] a thousand times daily, / meditating on the monkey who slays the host of demons and destroys sins.

1.74.s:
ayutaṃ prajapennityamacirājja yati dviṣam /
sugrīveṇa samaṃ rāmaṃ saṃdadhānaṃ kapiṃ smaran //
1.74.d:
अयुतं प्रजपेन्नित्यमचिराज्ज यति द्विषम् ।
सुग्रीवेण समं रामं संदधानं कपिं स्मरन् ॥
1.74.m: He should constantly recite ten thousand times, and soon he conquers his enemy. / Meditating on the monkey uniting Rāma with Sugrīva,

1.74.s:
prajapedayutaṃ yastu saṃdhiṃ kuryāddvipadvayoḥ /
dhyātvā laṅkāṃ dahṝntaṃ tamayutaṃ prajapenmanum //
1.74.d:
प्रजपेदयुतं यस्तु संधिं कुर्याद्द्विपद्वयोः ।
ध्यात्वा लङ्कां दहॄन्तं तमयुतं प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.74.m: he who recites ten thousand times brings about an alliance between two kings. / Meditating on him burning Laṅkā, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times;

1.74.s:
acirādeva śatrūṇāṃ grāmānsaṃpradahetsudhīḥ /
dhyātvā prayāṇasamaye hanumantaṃ japenmanum //
1.74.d:
अचिरादेव शत्रूणां ग्रामान्संप्रदहेत्सुधीः ।
ध्यात्वा प्रयाणसमये हनुमन्तं जपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.74.m: the wise man will soon burn down the villages of his enemies. / Meditating on Hanumān at the time of departure, one should recite the mantra;

1.74.s:
yo yāti so 'cirātsveṣṭaṃ sādhayitvā gṛhe vrajet /
hanumantaṃ sadā gehe yor'cayejjapatatparaḥ //
1.74.d:
यो याति सो ऽचिरात्स्वेष्टं साधयित्वा गृहे व्रजेत् ।
हनुमन्तं सदा गेहे योर्ऽचयेज्जपतत्परः ॥
1.74.m: he who departs will soon accomplish his desired goal and return home. / One who constantly worships Hanumān at home, intent on recitation,

1.74.s:
ārogyaṃ ca śriyaṃ kāntiṃ labhate nirupadravam /
kānane vyāghracaurebhyo rakṣenmanurayaṃ smṛtaḥ //
1.74.d:
आरोग्यं च श्रियं कान्तिं लभते निरुपद्रवम् ।
कानने व्याघ्रचौरेभ्यो रक्षेन्मनुरयं स्मृतः ॥
1.74.m: attains health, prosperity, and beauty, free from distress. / Remembered in the forest, this mantra protects from tigers and thieves.

1.74.s:
prasvāpakāle śayyāyāṃ smarenmantramananyadhīḥ /
tasya duḥsvapnacaurādibhayaṃ naiva bhavetkvacit //
1.74.d:
प्रस्वापकाले शय्यायां स्मरेन्मन्त्रमनन्यधीः ।
तस्य दुःस्वप्नचौरादिभयं नैव भवेत्क्वचित् ॥
1.74.m: At the time of falling asleep on the bed, one should remember the mantra with undivided mind; / he will never have any fear from bad dreams, thieves, or the like.

1.74.s:
viyatseṃdurhanumate tato rudrātmakāya ca /
varmāstrānto mahāmantro dvādaśārṇo 'ṣṭasiddhikṛt //
1.74.d:
वियत्सेंदुर्हनुमते ततो रुद्रात्मकाय च ।
वर्मास्त्रान्तो महामन्त्रो द्वादशार्णो ऽष्टसिद्धिकृत् ॥
1.74.m: Space with the moon [Haṃ], then "to Hanumān", and "to the essence of Rudra", / ending with the armor and weapon [Hūṃ Phaṭ]: this great twelve-syllabled mantra produces the eight spiritual accomplishments.

1.74.s:
rāmacandro muniścāsya jagatī chanda īritam /
hanumāndevatāṃ bījamādyaṃ śaktirhumīritā //
1.74.d:
रामचन्द्रो मुनिश्चास्य जगती छन्द ईरितम् ।
हनुमान्देवतां बीजमाद्यं शक्तिर्हुमीरिता ॥
1.74.m: Rāmacandra is its seer, and the metre is declared to be jagatī; / Hanumān is the deity, the first [syllable] is the seed-syllable, and Hūṃ is declared to be the power.

1.74.s:
ṣaḍdīrghabhājā bījena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret /
mahāśailaṃ samutpāṭya dhāvantaṃ rāvaṇaṃ prati //
1.74.d:
षड्दीर्घभाजा बीजेन षडङ्गानि समाचरेत् ।
महाशैलं समुत्पाट्य धावन्तं रावणं प्रति ॥
1.74.m: With the seed-syllable accompanied by the six long [vowels], one should perform the six limbs. / Uprooting a great mountain and charging towards Rāvaṇa,

1.74.s:
lākṣāraktāruṇaṃ raudraṃ kālāntakayamopamam /
jvaladagnisamaṃ jaitraṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham //
1.74.d:
लाक्षारक्तारुणं रौद्रं कालान्तकयमोपमम् ।
ज्वलदग्निसमं जैत्रं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ॥
1.74.m: red as lac and ruddy, fierce, like the Death of the end of time, / like blazing fire, victorious, possessing the radiance of ten million suns,

1.74.s:
aṅgadādyairmahāvīrairveṣṭitaṃ rudrarūpiṇam /
tiṣṭha tiṣṭha raṇe duṣṭa sṛjantaṃ ghoraniḥ svanam //
1.74.d:
अङ्गदाद्यैर्महावीरैर्वेष्टितं रुद्ररूपिणम् ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठ रणे दुष्ट सृजन्तं घोरनिः स्वनम् ॥
1.74.m: surrounded by great heroes such as Aṅgada, having the form of Rudra, / uttering a terrible roar: "Halt, halt in battle, evil one!" —

1.74.s:
śaivarūpiṇamabhyarcya dhyātvā lakṣa japenmanum /
daśāṃśaṃ juhuyādvīhīnpayodadhyājyamiśritān //
1.74.d:
शैवरूपिणमभ्यर्च्य ध्यात्वा लक्ष जपेन्मनुम् ।
दशांशं जुहुयाद्वीहीन्पयोदध्याज्यमिश्रितान् ॥
1.74.m: having meditated on and worshipped him in Śiva's form, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times. / One should offer a tenth part in fire oblations with rice mixed with milk, curd, and ghee.

1.74.s:
pūrvokte vaiṣṇave pīṭhe vimalādisamanvite /
mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlena pūjā kāryā hanūmataḥ //
1.74.d:
पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवे पीठे विमलादिसमन्विते ।
मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलेन पूजा कार्या हनूमतः ॥
1.74.m: On the previously described Vaiṣṇava seat endowed with Vimalā and others, / having formed the icon by means of the root mantra, the worship of Hanumān must be performed.

1.74.s:
dhyānaikamātro 'pi nṛṇāṃ siddhireva na saṃśayaḥ /
athāsya sādhanaṃ vakṣye lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
1.74.d:
ध्यानैकमात्रो ऽपि नृणां सिद्धिरेव न संशयः ।
अथास्य साधनं वक्ष्ये लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
1.74.m: Even by mere meditation, success is indeed attained by men; of this there is no doubt. / Now I shall declare his practice out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

1.74.s:
hanumatsādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam /
etadguhyatamaṃ loke śīghrasiddhikaraṃ param //
1.74.d:
हनुमत्साधनं पुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् ।
एतद्गुह्यतमं लोके शीघ्रसिद्धिकरं परम् ॥
1.74.m: The holy practice of Hanumān destroys heinous sins; / it is the most secret in the world, bringing swift success, supreme,

1.74.s:
mantrī yasya prasādena trailokyavijayī bhavet /
prātaḥ snātvā nadītīre upaviśya kuśāsane //
1.74.d:
मन्त्री यस्य प्रसादेन त्रैलोक्यविजयी भवेत् ।
प्रातः स्नात्वा नदीतीरे उपविश्य कुशासने ॥
1.74.m: by whose grace the practitioner of mantras becomes a conqueror of the three worlds. / Having bathed in the morning on a riverbank and sat down on a kuśa-grass seat,

1.74.s:
prāṇāyāmaṣaḍaṅge ca mūlena sakalaṃ caret /
puṣpāñjalyaṣṭakaṃ datvā dhyātvā rāmaṃ sasītakam //
1.74.d:
प्राणायामषडङ्गे च मूलेन सकलं चरेत् ।
पुष्पाञ्जल्यष्टकं दत्वा ध्यात्वा रामं ससीतकम् ॥
1.74.m: one should perform breath control, the six limbs, and all [rites] with the root mantra. / Having offered eight handfuls of flowers, and meditating on Rāma with Sītā,

1.74.s:
tāmrapātre tataḥ padmamaṣṭapatraṃ sakeśaram /
kucandanena ghṛṣṭena saṃlikhettacchalākayā //
1.74.d:
ताम्रपात्रे ततः पद्ममष्टपत्रं सकेशरम् ।
कुचन्दनेन घृष्टेन संलिखेत्तच्छलाकया ॥
1.74.m: he should then draw an eight-petaled lotus with filaments upon a copper plate / using ground red sandalwood with its stylus.

1.74.s:
karmikāyāṃ likhenmantraṃ tatrāvāhya kapīśvaram /
mūrtiṃ mūlena saṃkalpya dhyātvā pādyādikaṃ caret //
1.74.d:
कर्मिकायां लिखेन्मन्त्रं तत्रावाह्य कपीश्वरम् ।
मूर्तिं मूलेन संकल्प्य ध्यात्वा पाद्यादिकं चरेत् ॥
1.74.m: In the pericarp he should write the mantra, invoke the lord of monkeys there, / visualize the form with the root mantra, meditate, and offer water for the feet and other rites.

1.74.s:
gandhapuṣpādikaṃ sarvaṃ nivedya mūlamantrataḥ /
kesareṣu ṣaḍaṅgāni daleṣu ca tator'cayet //
1.74.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिकं सर्वं निवेद्य मूलमन्त्रतः ।
केसरेषु षडङ्गानि दलेषु च ततोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.74.m: Having offered all items such as perfume and flowers with the root mantra, / he should then worship the six limbs on the filaments and [the attendants] on the petals:

1.74.s:
sugrīvaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva hyaṅgadaṃ nalanīlakau /
jāṃbavantaṃ ca kumudaṃ kesarīśaṃ daler'cayet //
1.74.d:
सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणं चैव ह्यङ्गदं नलनीलकौ ।
जांबवन्तं च कुमुदं केसरीशं दलेर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.74.m: he should worship Sugrīva, Lakṣmaṇa, Aṅgada, Nala and Nīla, / Jāmbavān, Kumuda, and the lord Kesarin on the petals.

1.74.s:
dikpālāṃścāpi vajrādīnpūjayettadanantaram /
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayetsveṣṭamātmani //
1.74.d:
दिक्पालांश्चापि वज्रादीन्पूजयेत्तदनन्तरम् ।
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेत्स्वेष्टमात्मनि ॥
1.74.m: Immediately after that, he should also worship the guardians of the directions and their weapons such as the thunderbolt. / When the mantra is thus perfected, the practitioner of mantras accomplishes his desire within himself.

1.74.s:
nadītīre kānane vā parvate vijane 'thavā /
sādhayetsādhaka śreṣṭho bhūmigrahaṇapūrvakam //
1.74.d:
नदीतीरे कानने वा पर्वते विजने ऽथवा ।
साधयेत्साधक श्रेष्ठो भूमिग्रहणपूर्वकम् ॥
1.74.m: On a riverbank, or in a forest, or on a mountain, or in a solitary place, / the best practitioner should practice after taking possession of the ground,

1.74.s:
jitāhāro jitaśvāso jitavākca jitendriyaḥ /
digbandha nādikaṃ kṛtvā nyāsadhyānādipūrvakam //
1.74.d:
जिताहारो जितश्वासो जितवाक्च जितेन्द्रियः ।
दिग्बन्ध नादिकं कृत्वा न्यासध्यानादिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.74.m: having conquered food, conquered breath, conquered speech, and conquered the senses, / having performed the sealing of the directions and the rest preceded by ritual placement and meditation.

1.74.s:
lakṣaṃ japenmantrarājaṃ pūjayitvā tu pūrvavat /
lakṣānti divasaṃ prāpya kuryyāñca pūjanaṃ mahat //
1.74.d:
लक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रराजं पूजयित्वा तु पूर्ववत् ।
लक्षान्ति दिवसं प्राप्य कुर्य्याञ्च पूजनं महत् ॥
1.74.m: Having worshipped as before, he should recite the king of mantras one hundred thousand times; / and reaching the final day of the hundred thousand, he should perform a great worship.

1.74.s:
ekāgramanasā samyagdhyātvā pavananandanam /
divārātrau japaṃ kuryādyāvatsaṃdarśanaṃ bhavet //
1.74.d:
एकाग्रमनसा सम्यग्ध्यात्वा पवननन्दनम् ।
दिवारात्रौ जपं कुर्याद्यावत्संदर्शनं भवेत् ॥
1.74.m: Having meditated well upon the son of the wind with a one-pointed mind, / one should perform recitation day and night until an actual vision occurs.

1.74.s:
sudṛḍhaṃ sādhakaṃ matvā niśīthe pavanātmajaḥ /
suprasannastato bhūtvā prayāti sādhakāgrataḥ //
1.74.d:
सुदृढं साधकं मत्वा निशीथे पवनात्मजः ।
सुप्रसन्नस्ततो भूत्वा प्रयाति साधकाग्रतः ॥
1.74.m: Recognizing the practitioner to be firmly resolute, the son of the wind at midnight / becomes exceedingly pleased and appears before the practitioner.

1.74.s:
yathepsitaṃ varaṃ datvā sādhakāya kapīśvaraḥ /
varaṃ labdhvā sādhakandro viharedātmanaḥ sukhaiḥ //
1.74.d:
यथेप्सितं वरं दत्वा साधकाय कपीश्वरः ।
वरं लब्ध्वा साधकन्द्रो विहरेदात्मनः सुखैः ॥
1.74.m: Having granted the desired boon to the practitioner, the lord of monkeys [departs]; / having obtained the boon, the best among practitioners may wander about enjoying personal happiness.

1.74.s:
etaddhi sādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā /
prakāśitaṃ rahasyaṃ vai devānāmapi durlabham //
1.74.d:
एतद्धि साधनं पुण्यं लोकानां हितकाम्यया ।
प्रकाशितं रहस्यं वै देवानामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.74.m: For this meritorious practice, revealed out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds, / is indeed a secret difficult to attain even for the gods.

1.74.s:
anyānapiprayogāṃśca sādhayedātmano hitān /
viyadinduyutaṃ paścānṅeṃtaṃ pavananandanam //
1.74.d:
अन्यानपिप्रयोगांश्च साधयेदात्मनो हितान् ।
वियदिन्दुयुतं पश्चान्ङेंतं पवननन्दनम् ॥
1.74.m: He may also accomplish other applications beneficial to himself. / The ether [h] joined with the moon [ṃ], followed by 'pavananandana' ('son of the wind') in the dative case,

1.74.s:
vahnipriyānto mantro 'yaṃ daśārṇaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ /
munyādikaṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ ṣaḍaṅgānyapi pūrvavat //
1.74.d:
वह्निप्रियान्तो मन्त्रो ऽयं दशार्णः सर्वकामदः ।
मुन्यादिकं च पूर्वोक्तं षडङ्गान्यपि पूर्ववत् ॥
1.74.m: and ending with the beloved of fire [svāhā]—this ten-syllabled mantra grants all desires. / The seer and other [preliminaries] are as previously stated, and the six limbs are also as before.

1.74.s:
dhyāyedraṇe hanūmantaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham /
dhāvantaṃ rāvaṇaṃ jetuṃ dṛṣṭvā satvaramutthitam //
1.74.d:
ध्यायेद्रणे हनूमन्तं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ।
धावन्तं रावणं जेतुं दृष्ट्वा सत्वरमुत्थितम् ॥
1.74.m: One should meditate upon Hanūmān in battle, radiant as ten million suns, / who, having seen [the fallen], rose up swiftly to conquer the running Rāvaṇa;

1.74.s:
lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāvīraṃ patitaṃ raṇabhūtale /
guruṃ ca krodhamutpādya grahotuṃ guruparvatam //
1.74.d:
लक्ष्मणं च महावीरं पतितं रणभूतले ।
गुरुं च क्रोधमुत्पाद्य ग्रहोतुं गुरुपर्वतम् ॥
1.74.m: and, [seeing] the great hero Lakṣmaṇa fallen on the battlefield, / conceiving a mighty rage to seize the great mountain;

1.74.s:
hāhākāraiḥ sadarpaiśca kaṃpayantaṃ jagattrayam /
ābrahmāṇḍaṃ samākhyāpya kṛtvā bhīmaṃ kalevaram //
1.74.d:
हाहाकारैः सदर्पैश्च कंपयन्तं जगत्त्रयम् ।
आब्रह्माण्डं समाख्याप्य कृत्वा भीमं कलेवरम् ॥
1.74.m: causing the three worlds to tremble with haughty roars, / filling the cosmos [with his form], having assumed a terrifying body.

1.74.s:
lakṣaṃ japeddaśāṃśena juhuyātpūrvavatsudhīḥ /
pūrvavatpūjanaṃ proktaṃ mantra syāsya vidhānataḥ //
1.74.d:
लक्षं जपेद्दशांशेन जुहुयात्पूर्ववत्सुधीः ।
पूर्ववत्पूजनं प्रोक्तं मन्त्र स्यास्य विधानतः ॥
1.74.m: The wise man should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, and offer fire oblations with a tenth part as before; / worship is prescribed as before, according to the rule for this mantra.

1.74.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayedātmano hitam /
asyāpi mantravaryasya rahasyaṃ sādhanaṃ tu vai //
1.74.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेदात्मनो हितम् ।
अस्यापि मन्त्रवर्यस्य रहस्यं साधनं तु वै ॥
1.74.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner should accomplish his own welfare. / The secret practice of this excellent mantra as well,

1.74.s:
sugopyaṃ sarvatantreṣu na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit /
brāhme muhūrte cotthāya kṛtanityakriyaḥ śuciḥ //
1.74.d:
सुगोप्यं सर्वतन्त्रेषु न देयं यस्य कस्यचित् ।
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते चोत्थाय कृतनित्यक्रियः शुचिः ॥
1.74.m: which is to be guarded carefully in all tantras and not given to just anyone: / Rising at the hour of Brahman and purified, having performed his daily rites,

1.74.s:
gatvā nadīṃ taḥ snātvā tīrthamāvāhya cāṣṭadhā /
mūlamantraṃ tato japtvā siṃcedādityasaṃkhyayā //
1.74.d:
गत्वा नदीं तः स्नात्वा तीर्थमावाह्य चाष्टधा ।
मूलमन्त्रं ततो जप्त्वा सिंचेदादित्यसंख्यया ॥
1.74.m: having gone to a river and bathed there, having invoked the sacred ford eightfold, / and having then recited the root mantra, one should sprinkle [water] twelve times.

1.74.s:
evaṃ snānādikaṃ kṛtvā gaṅgātīre 'thavā punaḥ /
parvate vā vane vāpi bhūmigrahaṇapūrvakam //
1.74.d:
एवं स्नानादिकं कृत्वा गङ्गातीरे ऽथवा पुनः ।
पर्वते वा वने वापि भूमिग्रहणपूर्वकम् ॥
1.74.m: Having thus performed ablutions and the like, either on the bank of the Gaṅgā, / or on a mountain, or in a forest, having first taken possession of the ground,

1.74.s:
ādyavarṇaiḥ pūrakaṃ syātpañcavargaiśca kumbhakam /
recakaṃ ca punaryādyairevaṃ prāṇānniyanya ca //
1.74.d:
आद्यवर्णैः पूरकं स्यात्पञ्चवर्गैश्च कुम्भकम् ।
रेचकं च पुनर्याद्यैरेवं प्राणान्नियन्य च ॥
1.74.m: inhalation is done with the initial letters, retention with the five groups of consonants, / and exhalation again with the letters beginning with ya; thus restraining the breaths,

1.74.s:
vidhāya bhūtaśuddhyādi pīṭhanyāsāvadhi punaḥ /
dhyātvā pūrvoktavidhinā saṃpūjya ca kapīśvaram //
1.74.d:
विधाय भूतशुद्ध्यादि पीठन्यासावधि पुनः ।
ध्यात्वा पूर्वोक्तविधिना संपूज्य च कपीश्वरम् ॥
1.74.m: having performed the purification of elements and so forth up to the ritual placement on the seat, / and having meditated upon and worshipped the lord of monkeys according to the rule stated before,

1.74.s:
tadagre prajapennityaṃ sādhako 'yutamādarāt /
saptame divase prāpte kuryāñca pūjanaṃ mahat //
1.74.d:
तदग्रे प्रजपेन्नित्यं साधको ऽयुतमादरात् ।
सप्तमे दिवसे प्राप्ते कुर्याञ्च पूजनं महत् ॥
1.74.m: the practitioner should daily recite [the mantra] ten thousand times before him with reverence. / When the seventh day arrives, he should perform a great worship.

1.74.s:
ekāgramanasā mantrī divārātraṃ japenmanum /
mahābhayaṃ pradatvā tribhāgaśeṣāsu niścitam //
1.74.d:
एकाग्रमनसा मन्त्री दिवारात्रं जपेन्मनुम् ।
महाभयं प्रदत्वा त्रिभागशेषासु निश्चितम् ॥
1.74.m: With a one-pointed mind, the mantra-practitioner should recite the mantra day and night. / Having produced great dread, when a third of the night remains, certainly,

1.74.s:
yāminīṣu samāyāti niyataṃ pavanātmajaḥ /
yathepsitaṃ varaṃ dadyātsādhakāya kapīśvaraḥ //
1.74.d:
यामिनीषु समायाति नियतं पवनात्मजः ।
यथेप्सितं वरं दद्यात्साधकाय कपीश्वरः ॥
1.74.m: during the night watches, the son of the wind invariably arrives. / The lord of monkeys will grant the practitioner the boon he desires:

1.74.s:
vidyāṃ vāpi dhanaṃ vāpi rājyaṃ vā śatrunigraham /
tatkṣaṇādeva cāpnoti satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
1.74.d:
विद्यां वापि धनं वापि राज्यं वा शत्रुनिग्रहम् ।
तत्क्षणादेव चाप्नोति सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः ॥
1.74.m: whether knowledge, or wealth, or kingship, or the subjugation of enemies; / he obtains it immediately indeed; this is true, true, there is no doubt.

1.74.s:
iha loke 'khilānkāmānbhuktvānte muktimāpnuyāt /
sadyācitaṃ vāyuyugmaṃ hanūmanteti coddharet //
1.74.d:
इह लोके ऽखिलान्कामान्भुक्त्वान्ते मुक्तिमाप्नुयात् ।
सद्याचितं वायुयुग्मं हनूमन्तेति चोद्धरेत् ॥
1.74.m: Having enjoyed all desires in this world, he attains liberation in the end. / One should pronounce 'sadyācita', the pair of wind-syllables, and 'hanūmanta';

1.74.s:
phalānte phakriyānetrayuktā ca kāmikā tataḥ /
dhaggante dhagitetyuktvā āyurāsva padaṃ tataḥ //
1.74.d:
फलान्ते फक्रियानेत्रयुक्ता च कामिका ततः ।
धग्गन्ते धगितेत्युक्त्वा आयुरास्व पदं ततः ॥
1.74.m: after 'phala', [the letter] pha, kriyā, joined with the eyes, and then the wishing-cow; / after 'dhag', having said 'dhagita', then the word 'āyurāsva';

1.74.s:
lohito garuḍo hetibāṇanetrākṣaro manuḥ /
munyādikaṃ tu pūrvoktaṃ plīharogaharo hariḥ //
1.74.d:
लोहितो गरुडो हेतिबाणनेत्राक्षरो मनुः ।
मुन्यादिकं तु पूर्वोक्तं प्लीहरोगहरो हरिः ॥
1.74.m: red, Garuḍa, weapon, arrows, eyes—this is the mantra of [twenty-five] syllables. / The seer and others are as stated before; Hari, who removes spleen disease,

1.74.s:
devatā ca samuddiṣṭā plīhayuktodare punaḥ /
nāgavallīdalaṃ sthāpyamuparyācchādayettataḥ //
1.74.d:
देवता च समुद्दिष्टा प्लीहयुक्तोदरे पुनः ।
नागवल्लीदलं स्थाप्यमुपर्याच्छादयेत्ततः ॥
1.74.m: is declared to be the deity. Furthermore, upon the belly affected with spleen disease, / a betel leaf is to be placed, and then he should cover it from above

1.74.s:
vastraṃ caivāṣṭaguṇitaṃ tataḥ sādhakasattamaḥ /
śakalaṃ vaṃśajaṃ tasyopari muñcetkapiṃ smaret //
1.74.d:
वस्त्रं चैवाष्टगुणितं ततः साधकसत्तमः ।
शकलं वंशजं तस्योपरि मुञ्चेत्कपिं स्मरेत् ॥
1.74.m: with an eightfold folded cloth; then the excellent practitioner / should place a piece of bamboo on top of it, and remember the monkey.

1.74.s:
āraṇyasāṇakotpanne vahnau yaṣṭiṃ pratāpayet /
badarībhūruhotthāṃ tāṃ mantreṇānena saptadhā //
1.74.d:
आरण्यसाणकोत्पन्ने वह्नौ यष्टिं प्रतापयेत् ।
बदरीभूरुहोत्थां तां मन्त्रेणानेन सप्तधा ॥
1.74.m: In a fire produced from wild cow-dung, he should heat a stick / made from a jujube tree seven times with this mantra;

1.74.s:
tayā saṃtāḍayedvaṃśaśakalaṃ jaṭharasthitam /
saptakṛtvaḥ plīharogo nāśamāyāti niścitam //
1.74.d:
तया संताडयेद्वंशशकलं जठरस्थितम् ।
सप्तकृत्वः प्लीहरोगो नाशमायाति निश्चितम् ॥
1.74.m: with that [stick] he should strike the bamboo piece resting on the belly / seven times; the spleen disease is destroyed without a doubt.

1.74.s:
tāro namo bhagavate āñjaneyāya coñcaret /
amukasya śṛṅkhalāṃ troṭayadvitayamīrayet //
1.74.d:
तारो नमो भगवते आञ्जनेयाय चोञ्चरेत् ।
अमुकस्य शृङ्खलां त्रोटयद्वितयमीरयेत् ॥
1.74.m: One should utter the deliverer [oṃ], 'namo bhagavate āñjaneyāya' ('obeisance to the lord, son of Añjanā'), / 'amukasya śṛṅkhalāṃ' ('the chain of so-and-so'), and then pronounce the two words 'troṭaya troṭaya' ('break, break');

1.74.s:
bandhamokṣaṃ kuruyugaṃ svāhānto 'yaṃ manurmataḥ /
īśvaro 'sya muniśchando 'nuṣṭupca devatā punaḥ //
1.74.d:
बन्धमोक्षं कुरुयुगं स्वाहान्तो ऽयं मनुर्मतः ।
ईश्वरो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप्च देवता पुनः ॥
1.74.m: then 'bandha-mokṣaṃ kuru kuru' ('release from fetters, do, do'), ending with 'svāhā'—this is considered the mantra. / Īśvara is its seer, the metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity again

1.74.s:
śṛṅkhalāmocaraḥ śrīmānhanūmānpavanātmajaḥ /
haṃ bījaṃ ṭhadvayaṃ śaktirbandhamokṣe niyogatā //
1.74.d:
शृङ्खलामोचरः श्रीमान्हनूमान्पवनात्मजः ।
हं बीजं ठद्वयं शक्तिर्बन्धमोक्षे नियोगता ॥
1.74.m: is the glorious Hanūmān, the son of the wind, the breaker of chains. / 'Haṃ' is the seed-syllable, 'ṭha ṭha' is the power, and its application is in release from bonds.

1.74.s:
ṣaḍdīrghavahriyuktena bījenāṅgāni kalpayet /
vāme śailaṃ vairibhidaṃ viśuddhaṃ ṭaṅkamanyataḥ //
1.74.d:
षड्दीर्घवह्रियुक्तेन बीजेनाङ्गानि कल्पयेत् ।
वामे शैलं वैरिभिदं विशुद्धं टङ्कमन्यतः ॥
1.74.m: One should form the limbs with the seed-syllable joined with the six long vowels and the fire [r]. / In his left [hand] holding a rock, the destroyer of foes, and in the other a pure chisel,

1.74.s:
dadhānaṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ ca dhyāyetkuṇḍalinaṃ harim /
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣadaśāṃśaṃ cūtapallavaiḥ //
1.74.d:
दधानं स्वर्णवर्णं च ध्यायेत्कुण्डलिनं हरिम् ।
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षदशांशं चूतपल्लवैः ॥
1.74.m: golden-hued, one should meditate upon Hari wearing earrings. / Having thus meditated, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, and with a tenth of that, with mango leaves,

1.74.s:
juhuyātpūrvavatproktaṃ yajanaṃ vāsya sūribhiḥ /
mahākārāgṛhe prāpto hyayutaṃ prajapennaraḥ //
1.74.d:
जुहुयात्पूर्ववत्प्रोक्तं यजनं वास्य सूरिभिः ।
महाकारागृहे प्राप्तो ह्ययुतं प्रजपेन्नरः ॥
1.74.m: one should offer fire oblations; the worship is declared by the wise to be as before. / If a man has fallen into a great prison, he should recite it ten thousand times;

1.74.s:
śīghraṃ kārāgṛhānmuktaḥ sukhī bhavati niścitam /
yantraṃ cāsya pravakṣyāmi bandhamokṣakaraṃ śubham //
1.74.d:
शीघ्रं कारागृहान्मुक्तः सुखी भवति निश्चितम् ।
यन्त्रं चास्य प्रवक्ष्यामि बन्धमोक्षकरं शुभम् ॥
1.74.m: he is quickly released from the prison and becomes happy, undoubtedly. / I shall also describe his auspicious diagram that effects release from fetters:

1.74.s:
aṣṭacchadāntaḥ ṣaṭkoṇaṃ sādhyanāmasamanvitam /
ṣaṭkoṇeṣu dhruvaṃ ṅeṃtamāñjaneyapadaṃ likhet //
1.74.d:
अष्टच्छदान्तः षट्कोणं साध्यनामसमन्वितम् ।
षट्कोणेषु ध्रुवं ङेंतमाञ्जनेयपदं लिखेत् ॥
1.74.m: A hexagon inside an eight-petalled [lotus], accompanied by the name of the person to be affected; / in the six angles one should write the fixed syllable [oṃ] and the word 'āñjaneya' in the dative case;

1.74.s:
aṣṭacchadeṣu vilikhetpraṇavo vātuvātviti /
gorocanākuṅkumena likhitvā yantramuttamam //
1.74.d:
अष्टच्छदेषु विलिखेत्प्रणवो वातुवात्विति ।
गोरोचनाकुङ्कुमेन लिखित्वा यन्त्रमुत्तमम् ॥
1.74.m: on the eight petals one should write the praṇava, and 'vātu vātu'. / Having drawn this excellent diagram with yellow pigment and saffron,

1.74.s:
dhṛtvā mūrdhni japenmantramayutaṃ bandhamuktaye /
yantrametallikhitvā tu mṛttikopari mārjayet //
1.74.d:
धृत्वा मूर्ध्नि जपेन्मन्त्रमयुतं बन्धमुक्तये ।
यन्त्रमेतल्लिखित्वा तु मृत्तिकोपरि मार्जयेत् ॥
1.74.m: wearing it on the head, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times for release from bonds. / Or, having drawn this diagram, the knower of mantras should wipe it over the clay

1.74.s:
dakṣahastena mantrajñaḥ pratyahaṃ maṇḍalā vadhi /
evaṃ kṛte mahākārāgṛhānmantrī vimucyate //
1.74.d:
दक्षहस्तेन मन्त्रज्ञः प्रत्यहं मण्डला वधि ।
एवं कृते महाकारागृहान्मन्त्री विमुच्यते ॥
1.74.m: with his right hand every day for the period of a sacred diagram [forty-eight days]. / When this is done, the mantra-practitioner is freed from the great prison.

1.74.s:
gaganaṃ jvalanaḥ sākṣī markaṭeti dvayaṃ tataḥ /
toyaṃ śaśeṣe makare parimuñcati muñcati //
1.74.d:
गगनं ज्वलनः साक्षी मर्कटेति द्वयं ततः ।
तोयं शशेषे मकरे परिमुञ्चति मुञ्चति ॥
1.74.m: The sky [ha], fire [ra], the witness, then two times 'markaṭa' ('monkey'); / water [va], then in the crocodile, 'parimuñcati muñcati' ('releases, releases');

1.74.s:
tataḥ śṛṅkhalikāṃ ceti vedanetrākṣaro manuḥ /
imaṃ mantraṃ dakṣakare likhitvā vāmahastataḥ //
1.74.d:
ततः शृङ्खलिकां चेति वेदनेत्राक्षरो मनुः ।
इमं मन्त्रं दक्षकरे लिखित्वा वामहस्ततः ॥
1.74.m: then 'śṛṅkhalikāṃ' ('the fetter')—this is the mantra of twenty-four syllables. / Having written this mantra on the right hand, with the left hand

1.74.s:
dūrikṛtya japenmantramaṣṭottaraśataṃ budhaḥ /
trisaptāhātprabaddho 'sau mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.74.d:
दूरिकृत्य जपेन्मन्त्रमष्टोत्तरशतं बुधः ।
त्रिसप्ताहात्प्रबद्धो ऽसौ मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.74.m: wiping it away, the wise man should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times. / Within three weeks, he who was bound is freed; of this there is no doubt.

1.74.s:
munyādyarcādikaṃ sarvamasya pūrvavadācaret /
lakṣaṃ japo daśāṃśena śubhairdravyaiśca homayet //
1.74.d:
मुन्याद्यर्चादिकं सर्वमस्य पूर्ववदाचरेत् ।
लक्षं जपो दशांशेन शुभैर्द्रव्यैश्च होमयेत् ॥
1.74.m: One should perform the worship of the sage and others for this [mantra] as before. / Recitation is one hundred thousand, and one should offer fire oblations with tenth part [of that number] using auspicious substances.

1.74.s:
pucchākāre suvastre ca lekhanyā kṣurakotthayā /
gandhāṣṭakairlikhedvūpaṃ kapirājasya sundaram //
1.74.d:
पुच्छाकारे सुवस्त्रे च लेखन्या क्षुरकोत्थया ।
गन्धाष्टकैर्लिखेद्वूपं कपिराजस्य सुन्दरम् ॥
1.74.m: On a fine cloth shaped like a tail, with a pen made of kṣuraka, / one should draw the handsome form of the monkey king using the eight scents.

1.74.s:
tanmadhye 'ṣṭadaśārṇaṃ tu śatrunāmānvitaṃ likhet /
tena mantrābhijaptena śirobaddhvena bhūmipaḥ //
1.74.d:
तन्मध्ये ऽष्टदशार्णं तु शत्रुनामान्वितं लिखेत् ।
तेन मन्त्राभिजप्तेन शिरोबद्ध्वेन भूमिपः ॥
1.74.m: In its middle, one should write the eighteen-syllable [mantra] accompanied by the enemy's name. / A king, having bound that [cloth] consecrated by recitation upon his head,

1.74.s:
jayatyarigaṇaṃ sarvaṃ darśanādeva niścitam /
candrasūryo parāgādau pūrvoktaṃ lekhayeddhvaje //
1.74.d:
जयत्यरिगणं सर्वं दर्शनादेव निश्चितम् ।
चन्द्रसूर्यो परागादौ पूर्वोक्तं लेखयेद्ध्वजे ॥
1.74.m: certainly conquers the whole host of enemies merely by its sight. / At the time of a solar or lunar eclipse and the like, one should have what was spoken before written upon a banner.

1.74.s:
dhvajamādāya mantrajñaḥ saṃsparśānmokṣaṇāvadhi /
mātṛkāṃ jāpayetpaścāddaśāṃśena ca homayet //
1.74.d:
ध्वजमादाय मन्त्रज्ञः संस्पर्शान्मोक्षणावधि ।
मातृकां जापयेत्पश्चाद्दशांशेन च होमयेत् ॥
1.74.m: Taking the banner, the knower of mantras should recite the mātṛkā / from the moment of contact [of the eclipse] until the end of liberation [from it], and then make fire oblations with a tenth part [of the count].

1.74.s:
tilaiḥ sarṣapasaṃmiśraiḥ saṃskṛte havyavāhane /
gaje dhvajaṃ samāropya gacchedyuddhvāya bhūpatiḥ //
1.74.d:
तिलैः सर्षपसंमिश्रैः संस्कृते हव्यवाहने ।
गजे ध्वजं समारोप्य गच्छेद्युद्ध्वाय भूपतिः ॥
1.74.m: With sesame seeds mixed with mustard seeds into the consecrated sacrificial fire. / Mounting the banner upon an elephant, the king should go to battle.

1.74.s:
gajasthaṃ taṃ dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyante 'rayo dhruvam /
mahārakṣākaraṃ yantraṃ vakṣye samyagdhanūmataḥ //
1.74.d:
गजस्थं तं ध्वजं दृष्ट्वा पलायन्ते ऽरयो ध्रुवम् ।
महारक्षाकरं यन्त्रं वक्ष्ये सम्यग्धनूमतः ॥
1.74.m: Seeing that banner mounted upon an elephant, the enemies certainly flee. / I shall explain fully the yantra of Hanūmat that produces great protection:

1.74.s:
likhedvasudalaṃ padmaṃ sādhyākhyāyutakarṇikam /
dale 'ṣṭakoṇamālikhya mālāmantreṇa veṣṭayet //
1.74.d:
लिखेद्वसुदलं पद्मं साध्याख्यायुतकर्णिकम् ।
दले ऽष्टकोणमालिख्य मालामन्त्रेण वेष्टयेत् ॥
1.74.m: One should draw an eight-petalled lotus whose pericarp contains the name of the one to be mastered. / Having drawn an eight-pointed figure on the petal[s], one should encircle it with the mālāmantra.

1.74.s:
tadbahir māyayāveṣṭya prāṇasthāpanamācaret /
likhitaṃ svarṇalekhanyā bhūrjapatre suśobhane //
1.74.d:
तद्बहिर् माययावेष्ट्य प्राणस्थापनमाचरेत् ।
लिखितं स्वर्णलेखन्या भूर्जपत्रे सुशोभने ॥
1.74.m: Having encircled it outside with Māyā, one should perform the installation of the breath of life. / Drawn with a golden pen on very splendid birch-bark,

1.74.s:
kāśmīrarocanābhyāṃ tu trilohena ca veṣṭitam /
sampātasādhitaṃ yantraṃ bhuje vā mūrdhni dhārayet //
1.74.d:
काश्मीररोचनाभ्यां तु त्रिलोहेन च वेष्टितम् ।
सम्पातसाधितं यन्त्रं भुजे वा मूर्ध्नि धारयेत् ॥
1.74.m: with saffron and yellow orpiment, and enclosed in three metals, / the yantra, consecrated through repeated offerings, should be worn on the arm or the head.

1.74.s:
raṇe durodare vāde vyavahāre jayaṃ labhet /
grahairvighnairviṣaiḥ śastraiścaurairnaivābhibhūyate //
1.74.d:
रणे दुरोदरे वादे व्यवहारे जयं लभेत् ।
ग्रहैर्विघ्नैर्विषैः शस्त्रैश्चौरैर्नैवाभिभूयते ॥
1.74.m: In battle, in gambling, in debate, and in worldly transactions, he obtains victory; / he is never overcome by seizing spirits, obstacles, poisons, weapons, or thieves.

1.74.s:
sarvānro gānapākṛtya ciraṃ jīvecchataṃ samāḥ /
ṣaḍdīrghayuktaṃ gagana vahnyākhyaṃ tārasaṃpuṭam //
1.74.d:
सर्वान्रो गानपाकृत्य चिरं जीवेच्छतं समाः ।
षड्दीर्घयुक्तं गगन वह्न्याख्यं तारसंपुटम् ॥
1.74.m: Warding off all diseases, he lives long for a hundred years. / The sky accompanied by the six long [vowels], designated as fire, enclosed by the praṇava—

1.74.s:
aṣṭārṇo 'yaṃ mahāmantro mālāmantro 'tha kathyate /
praṇavo vajrakāyeti vajratuṇḍeti saṃpaṭhet //
1.74.d:
अष्टार्णो ऽयं महामन्त्रो मालामन्त्रो ऽथ कथ्यते ।
प्रणवो वज्रकायेति वज्रतुण्डेति संपठेत् ॥
1.74.m: this is the eight-syllable great mantra. Now the garland-mantra is spoken: / The praṇava; one should recite 'vajrakāya', 'vajratuṇḍa';

1.74.s:
kapilānte piṅgaleti urddhvakeśamahāpadam /
balaraktamukhānte tu taḍijjihva mahā tataḥ //
1.74.d:
कपिलान्ते पिङ्गलेति उर्द्ध्वकेशमहापदम् ।
बलरक्तमुखान्ते तु तडिज्जिह्व महा ततः ॥
1.74.m: after 'kapila', 'piṅgala', the great words 'ūrdhvakeśa', / then after 'balaraktamukha', 'taḍijjihva mahā';

1.74.s:
raudradaṃṣṭrotkaṭaṃ paścātkahadvandvaṃ karāliti /
mahadṛḍhaprahāreṇa laṅkeśvaravadhāttataḥ //
1.74.d:
रौद्रदंष्ट्रोत्कटं पश्चात्कहद्वन्द्वं करालिति ।
महदृढप्रहारेण लङ्केश्वरवधात्ततः ॥
1.74.m: then 'raudradaṃṣṭrotkaṭa', the pair of 'kaha', 'karālin', / then 'mahadṛḍhaprahāreṇa laṅkeśvaravadhāt';

1.74.s:
vāyurmahāsetupadaṃ bandhānte ca mahā punaḥ /
śailapravāha gaganecara ehyehi saṃvadet //
1.74.d:
वायुर्महासेतुपदं बन्धान्ते च महा पुनः ।
शैलप्रवाह गगनेचर एह्येहि संवदेत् ॥
1.74.m: the word 'vāyurmahāsetu' and after 'bandha', again 'mahā', / one should say 'śailapravāha gaganecara ehyehi';

1.74.s:
bhagavanmahābalānte parākramapadaṃ vadet /
bhairavājñāpayaihyehi mahāraudrapadaṃ tataḥ //
1.74.d:
भगवन्महाबलान्ते पराक्रमपदं वदेत् ।
भैरवाज्ञापयैह्येहि महारौद्रपदं ततः ॥
1.74.m: after 'bhagavanmahābala', one should speak the word 'parākrama'; / 'bhairavājñāpaya ehyehi', then the word 'mahāraudra';

1.74.s:
dīrghapucchena varṇānte vadedveṣṭaya vairiṇam /
jaṃbhayadvayamābhāṣya varmāstrānto manurmataḥ //
1.74.d:
दीर्घपुच्छेन वर्णान्ते वदेद्वेष्टय वैरिणम् ।
जंभयद्वयमाभाष्य वर्मास्त्रान्तो मनुर्मतः ॥
1.74.m: after the syllables 'dīrghapucchena', one should say 'veṣṭaya vairiṇam', / and having spoken the pair of 'jambhaya', the mantra ends in armor and weapon.

1.74.s:
mālāhvayo dvijaśreṣṭha śaranetradharākṣaraḥ /
mālāmantrāṣṭārṇayośca munyādyarcā tu pūrvavat //
1.74.d:
मालाह्वयो द्विजश्रेष्ठ शरनेत्रधराक्षरः ।
मालामन्त्राष्टार्णयोश्च मुन्याद्यर्चा तु पूर्ववत् ॥
1.74.m: Called the garland-mantra, O best among the twice-born, it has one hundred and twenty-five syllables. / The worship of the sage and others for the garland-mantra and the eight-syllable [mantra] is as before.

1.74.s:
japto yuddhe jayaṃ dadyādvyādhau vyādhivināśanaḥ /
evaṃ yo bhajate mantrī vāyuputraṃ kapīśvaram //
1.74.d:
जप्तो युद्धे जयं दद्याद्व्याधौ व्याधिविनाशनः ।
एवं यो भजते मन्त्री वायुपुत्रं कपीश्वरम् ॥
1.74.m: Recited, it grants victory in battle; in illness, it destroys disease. / Thus, the mantra-practitioner who worships the son of the wind, the lord of monkeys,

1.74.s:
sarvānsa labhate kāmānde vairapi sudurlabhān /
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutānpautrānsaubhāgyamatulaṃ yaśaḥ //
1.74.d:
सर्वान्स लभते कामान्दे वैरपि सुदुर्लभान् ।
धनं धान्यं सुतान्पौत्रान्सौभाग्यमतुलं यशः ॥
1.74.m: obtains all desires that are very hard to attain even for the gods: / wealth, grain, sons, grandsons, unparalleled good fortune, renown,

1.74.s:
medhāṃ vidyāṃ prabhāṃ rājyaṃ vivāde vijayaṃ tathā /
vaśyādyāni ca karmāṇi saṃgare vijayaṃ tathā //
1.74.d:
मेधां विद्यां प्रभां राज्यं विवादे विजयं तथा ।
वश्याद्यानि च कर्माणि संगरे विजयं तथा ॥
1.74.m: intellect, learning, splendor, sovereignty, as well as victory in dispute, / rituals such as subjection, and likewise victory in battle.

1.74.s:
upāsitoṃ'janāgarbhasaṃbhūtaḥ pradadātyalam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne sanatkumāravibhāge tṛtīyapāde hanumanmantrakathanaṃnāma catuḥsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.74.d:
उपासितोंऽजनागर्भसंभूतः प्रददात्यलम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने सनत्कुमारविभागे तृतीयपादे हनुमन्मन्त्रकथनंनाम चतुःसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
1.74.m:
Worshipped, the one born from the womb of Añjanā abundantly bestows [these].

Thus, in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa, in the first part, in the great narrative, in the section of Sanatkumāra, in the third quarter, the seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Explanation of the Hanūmat-mantra'.

1.75.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
atha dīpavidhiṃ vakṣye sarahasyaṃ hanūmataḥ /
yasya vijñānamātreṇa siddho bhavati sādhakaḥ //
1.75.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथ दीपविधिं वक्ष्ये सरहस्यं हनूमतः ।
यस्य विज्ञानमात्रेण सिद्धो भवति साधकः ॥
1.75.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall explain the rite of the lamp of Hanūmat together with its secret, / by the mere understanding of which the practitioner becomes perfected.

1.75.s:
dīpapātrapramāṇaṃ ca tailamānaṃ krameṇa tu /
dravyasya ca pramāṇaṃ vai tattu mānamanukramāt //
1.75.d:
दीपपात्रप्रमाणं च तैलमानं क्रमेण तु ।
द्रव्यस्य च प्रमाणं वै तत्तु मानमनुक्रमात् ॥
1.75.m: The measurement of the lamp-vessel and the measure of oil in due order, / and the measurement of the substance—that measurement in succession,

1.75.s:
sthānabhedaṃ ca mantraṃ ca dīpadānamanuṃ pṛthak /
puṣpavāsitatailena sarvakāmapradaṃ matam //
1.75.d:
स्थानभेदं च मन्त्रं च दीपदानमनुं पृथक् ।
पुष्पवासिततैलेन सर्वकामप्रदं मतम् ॥
1.75.m: the variation of places, the mantra, and separately the mantra for offering the lamp. / [A lamp] with flower-scented oil is considered to grant all desires.

1.75.s:
tilatailaṃ śriyaḥ prāptyai pathikāgamanaṃ prati /
atasītailamuddiṣṭaṃ vaśyakarmaṇi niścitam //
1.75.d:
तिलतैलं श्रियः प्राप्त्यै पथिकागमनं प्रति ।
अतसीतैलमुद्दिष्टं वश्यकर्मणि निश्चितम् ॥
1.75.m: Sesame oil is for obtaining prosperity; for the arrival of a traveler, / linseed oil is prescribed, [and] certainly in the act of subjugation.

1.75.s:
sārṣāpaṃ roganāśāya kathitaṃ karmakovidaiḥ /
māraṇe rājikotthaṃ vā vibhītakasamudbhavam //
1.75.d:
सार्षापं रोगनाशाय कथितं कर्मकोविदैः ।
मारणे राजिकोत्थं वा विभीतकसमुद्भवम् ॥
1.75.m: Mustard oil is declared for the destruction of diseases by those skilled in rituals; / in eradication, [oil] from black mustard seeds or derived from vibhītaka [is used];

1.75.s:
uñcāṭane karajotthaṃ vidveṣe madhuvṛkṣajam /
alābhe sarvatailānāṃ tilajaṃ tailamuttamam //
1.75.d:
उञ्चाटने करजोत्थं विद्वेषे मधुवृक्षजम् ।
अलाभे सर्वतैलानां तिलजं तैलमुत्तमम् ॥
1.75.m: in expulsion, [oil] derived from karaja; in causing hatred, that produced from the madhūka tree. / If all oils are unavailable, sesame-derived oil is best.

1.75.s:
godhūmāśca tilā māṣā mudgā vai taṇḍulāḥ kramāt /
pañcadhānyamidaṃ proktaṃ nityadīpaṃ tu māruteḥ //
1.75.d:
गोधूमाश्च तिला माषा मुद्गा वै तण्डुलाः क्रमात् ।
पञ्चधान्यमिदं प्रोक्तं नित्यदीपं तु मारुतेः ॥
1.75.m: Wheat, sesame, black gram, green gram, and rice in order— / this is declared to be the five grains for the daily lamp of the son of the wind.

1.75.s:
pañcadhānyasamudbhūtaṃ piṣṭamātraṃ suśobhanam /
sarvakāmapradaṃ proktaṃ sarvadā dīpadānake //
1.75.d:
पञ्चधान्यसमुद्भूतं पिष्टमात्रं सुशोभनम् ।
सर्वकामप्रदं प्रोक्तं सर्वदा दीपदानके ॥
1.75.m: Merely flour produced from the five grains, being very auspicious, / is declared to grant all desires in always offering lamps.

1.75.s:
vaśye taḍulapiṣṭotthaṃ māraṇe māṣapiṣṭajam /
uñcāṭane kṛṣṇatilapiṣṭajaṃ ca prakīrtitam //
1.75.d:
वश्ये तडुलपिष्टोत्थं मारणे माषपिष्टजम् ।
उञ्चाटने कृष्णतिलपिष्टजं च प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.75.m: In subjugation, [a lamp-vessel] made of rice flour [is prescribed]; in eradication, made of black gram flour; / in expulsion, it is proclaimed to be made of black sesame flour;

1.75.s:
pathikāgamane proktaṃ godhūmotthaṃ sataṇḍulam /
mohane tvāḍhakījāta vidveṣe ca kulatthajam //
1.75.d:
पथिकागमने प्रोक्तं गोधूमोत्थं सतण्डुलम् ।
मोहने त्वाढकीजात विद्वेषे च कुलत्थजम् ॥
1.75.m: in the arrival of a traveler, [a vessel] made of wheat with rice is declared; / in bewitchment, produced from pigeon pea; and in causing hatred, made of horse gram.

1.75.s:
saṃgrāme kevalā māṣāḥ proktā dīpasya pātrake /
saṃdhau tripiṣṭajaṃ lakṣmīhetoḥ kastūrikābhavam //
1.75.d:
संग्रामे केवला माषाः प्रोक्ता दीपस्य पात्रके ।
संधौ त्रिपिष्टजं लक्ष्मीहेतोः कस्तूरिकाभवम् ॥
1.75.m: In battle, black gram alone is declared for the vessel of the lamp; / in peacemaking, [a vessel] made of three flours; for the sake of prosperity, that which is made of musk,

1.75.s:
elālavaṅgakarpūramṛganābhisamudbhavam /
kanyāprāptyai tathā rājavaṃśye sakhye tathaiva ca //
1.75.d:
एलालवङ्गकर्पूरमृगनाभिसमुद्भवम् ।
कन्याप्राप्त्यै तथा राजवंश्ये सख्ये तथैव च ॥
1.75.m: or produced with cardamom, clove, camphor, and musk, / likewise for obtaining a maiden, in matters of royal lineage, and likewise in friendship.

1.75.s:
alābhe sarvavastūnāṃ pañcadhānyaṃ varaṃ smṛtam /
aṣṭamuṣṭirbhavetkiñcitkiñcidaṣṭau caḥ puṣkalam //
1.75.d:
अलाभे सर्ववस्तूनां पञ्चधान्यं वरं स्मृतम् ।
अष्टमुष्टिर्भवेत्किञ्चित्किञ्चिदष्टौ चः पुष्कलम् ॥
1.75.m: In the absence of all materials, the five grains are remembered as best. / Eight handfuls make a kiñcit, and eight kiñcits make a puṣkala.

1.75.s:
puṣkalānāṃ caturṇāṃ ca hyāḍhakaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
caturāḍhako bhaveddroṇaḥ khārī droṇacatuṣṭayam //
1.75.d:
पुष्कलानां चतुर्णां च ह्याढकः परिकीर्तितः ।
चतुराढको भवेद्द्रोणः खारी द्रोणचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.75.m: Four puṣkalas are proclaimed as an āḍhaka; / four āḍhakas make a droṇa, and a khārī is four droṇas.

1.75.s:
khārīcatuṣṭaya prasthasaṃjñā ca parikīrtitā /
athavānyaprakāreṇa mānamatra nigadyate //
1.75.d:
खारीचतुष्टय प्रस्थसंज्ञा च परिकीर्तिता ।
अथवान्यप्रकारेण मानमत्र निगद्यते ॥
1.75.m: Four khārīs are proclaimed by the designation prastha. / Or rather, by another method, the measure here is declared:

1.75.s:
paladvayaṃ tu prasṛtaṃ dviguṇaṃ kuḍavaṃ matam /
caturbhiḥ kuḍavaiḥ prasthastaiścaturbhistathāḍhakaḥ //
1.75.d:
पलद्वयं तु प्रसृतं द्विगुणं कुडवं मतम् ।
चतुर्भिः कुडवैः प्रस्थस्तैश्चतुर्भिस्तथाढकः ॥
1.75.m: Two palas make a prasṛta, and twice that is considered a kuḍava; / four kuḍavas make a prastha, and by four of those likewise an āḍhaka;

1.75.s:
caturāḍhako bhaveddroṇaḥṛ khārī droṇacatuṣṭayam /
krameṇaitena te jñeyāḥ pātre ṣaṭkarmasaṃbhave //
1.75.d:
चतुराढको भवेद्द्रोणःऋ खारी द्रोणचतुष्टयम् ।
क्रमेणैतेन ते ज्ञेयाः पात्रे षट्कर्मसंभवे ॥
1.75.m: four āḍhakas make a droṇa, and a khārī is four droṇas. / In this order they are to be known for a vessel used in the six magical rites.

1.75.s:
pañca sapta nava tathā pramāṇāste yathākramam /
saugandhe naiva mānaṃ syāttadyathāruci saṃmatam //
1.75.d:
पञ्च सप्त नव तथा प्रमाणास्ते यथाक्रमम् ।
सौगन्धे नैव मानं स्यात्तद्यथारुचि संमतम् ॥
1.75.m: Five, seven, and nine are their measures respectively; / for fragrant substance there is no fixed measure, it is approved according to taste.

1.75.s:
nityapātre tu tailānāṃ niyamo vārtikodbhavaḥ /
